does_not_fit_when: Checks are advisory by policy and a red pipeline is routinely merged past
There is no CI, in which case the lifecycle commands still work but the last link of every chain is missing
fits_when: A completion claim should require verification that actually ran, with its exit code recorded
Public capability claims are expected to name their implementation and their test
The pipeline must fail when a declared rule stops being invoked

does_not_fit_when: The work is a single sitting and nothing needs to be recalled afterwards

fits_when: Decisions need to be findable later by the task and commit that made them
Progress must be quotable without reading everything that led to it
Something unresolved should block acceptance until it is answered
facts.summary: A task spans days, several sessions, or several people, and the reasoning has to survive the gaps.

The layer's objects are worth exposing as resources and tools rather than as files a client may or may not open

nodes.label: docs/claims/why-diagnosis-explainable.md

nodes.label: docs/claims/why-references-resolve.md

nodes.label: docs/claims/wiring-reconciliation.md

facts.headline: A change runs the gates its paths can affect, every gate is the same script a person runs, and the public site is published only from a commit whose derived data proved current.

nodes.label: cockpit
nodes.summary: The Cockpit: the registry rendered for a person

nodes.label: context
nodes.summary: Every directory of the layer carries its contract, and a worker reads what applies

nodes.label: continuity

nodes.label: coordination
nodes.summary: Several agents on one repository, without stepping on each other

facts.headline: Every worker declares the paths it may touch, every session can see who else is attached and what they announced, and a collision is reported before it is committed.

nodes.label: declare-once
nodes.summary: Declare once, derive every interface

facts.headline: A capability is written in one place, and the command line, the HTTP API, the OpenAPI document, MCP, the Cockpit, the reference and this website are projections of it.

nodes.label: deployments

facts.headline: The port, the routes, the resources and the build inputs of a hosted executable are stated once, and the container definition and the provider configuration are projections that cannot drift from it.

nodes.label: doctrine
nodes.summary: Rules a machine decides, wired, tested and CI-blocking

nodes.label: finish-contract
nodes.summary: Done is a contract, evaluated line by line and refused when unmet

facts.headline: A worker does not get to define its own successful completion: every line of the finish contract is printed pass or fail, and nothing is written to the record until all of them pass.

nodes.label: install
nodes.summary: One command to install, one to initialise, nothing else to trust

facts.headline: The installer downloads one archive for your machine, verifies its digest against the release metadata before unpacking anything, and installs atomically; no git, no Rust, no Node, no root.

nodes.label: interfaces
nodes.summary: One registry over the command line, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI and MCP

facts.headline: Every agent, script and person reads the same repository through the interface it already speaks, and none of the interfaces is maintained by hand.

nodes.label: knowledge
nodes.summary: Decisions and knowledge that compound instead of evaporating

facts.headline: What was decided, why, and what was rejected is recorded where the next session reads it, and a durable decision becomes an architecture record with typed links to what it put in force.

nodes.label: planning
nodes.summary: Milestones and issues as data; status derived, never stored

facts.headline: An issue records what happened to it and the engine derives whether it is blocked, ready, active, verifying or done from the dependency graph, so the roadmap cannot disagree with the plan.

nodes.label: policy
nodes.summary: One policy, projected into every tool's instruction file

nodes.label: provenance
nodes.summary: Every record names the commit, the branch and the episode that made it

facts.headline: Who did what, under which task, at which commit, in which session is a ledger the tool writes and a person can read back, not a memory of a conversation.

nodes.label: skills
nodes.summary: Skills are procedures as data, discovered and checked, never registered

facts.headline: A skill is one directory under the layer; adding it is the whole act, and the command line, the website and MCP all read it from the same file.

nodes.label: use-cases
nodes.summary: Every use case is executed against the tool, not described

facts.headline: What a person does with the tool is one file with a scenario the tool runs against itself; the page shows that execution, and a public command no use case runs is a gap the tool reports.

nodes.label: why
nodes.summary: The failure modes it answers are objects, not marketing pages

nodes.label: worktrees
nodes.summary: One branch, one worktree, at a path derived from git

facts.headline: A branch's worktree is where git says it is, never where somebody chose to put it, and a misplaced one is a diagnostic with a remedy rather than a mystery.

nodes.label: I0001
nodes.summary: Audit what actually plans work in this repository

acceptance_criteria: The GitHub milestone and issue inventory is measured, not assumed
The existing canonical-to-derived pipeline is identified so the new model reuses it
The portability constraints that bound the implementation are named
facts.current_state: Planning lived in task records, handovers, checkpoints and decisions. GitHub had no milestones and no issues. There was no dependency relation between pieces of work anywhere.
facts.desired_state: The current-state map exists, backed by commands anyone can rerun, and the schema work that follows cites it.
non_scope: Any change to behaviour
facts.objective: Establish an evidence-backed map of how work is currently planned, tracked and remembered here, so that the model that replaces it is built against reality rather than against the README.
facts.risk: Low. Read-only.

nodes.label: I0002
nodes.summary: Define the canonical milestone and issue schema

acceptance_criteria: An unknown key in a milestone or issue file is a reported failure
No status field exists in either schema
Evidence is part of the record whose completion it gates
facts.current_state: Policy, profiles and prompts each have an allowlist under share/allow. Milestones and issues had none because they did not exist.
facts.desired_state: share/allow/project.txt, share/allow/milestone.txt and share/allow/issue.txt exist and every key in a canonical file matches one of them.
non_scope: JSON Schema; this repository validates with allowlists and its own YAML subset
A separate evidence directory; evidence lives inside the record it proves
facts.risk: A schema too small forces a later migration; a schema too large invites fields nobody reads.
facts.why: Every surface downstream reads these files. A field that is written and never read, or read and never written, becomes a lie that the website eventually publishes.

nodes.label: I0003
nodes.summary: Implement the model loader and the status derivation engine

acceptance_criteria: Issue status is derived from started_at, verified_at, completed_at, cancelled, evidence coverage and dependency state
Milestone status is derived from its issues and its own evidence
The active milestone is derived from order and status, not declared
A completed issue whose required evidence is missing derives VERIFY, not DONE
facts.current_state: Nothing read the canonical files.
facts.desired_state: lib/project.sh loads the files, lib/project.awk derives the model, and the CLI, the site generator and the GitHub adapter all read that model.
non_scope: Any status field a human can set directly
facts.objective: Load every canonical file into one normalised model and derive issue and milestone status from recorded facts, in exactly one implementation that every surface calls.
facts.risk: bash 3.2 has no associative arrays; the graph work is done in awk, which does.
facts.why: Four surfaces need to know what is READY. Four implementations of READY is four answers. One engine is the whole architecture.

nodes.label: I0004
nodes.summary: Implement DAG validation and execution waves

acceptance_criteria: A cycle is detected and the issues inside it are named
A self-dependency and an unknown dependency are each a distinct finding
Waves place an issue one layer past its deepest dependency
Two issues sharing a wave and a scope path are reported as serialised
facts.current_state: No graph existed.
facts.desired_state: Unknown, self and duplicate dependencies, duplicate ids and cycles are each rejected by name, and waves are computed by Kahn layering.
non_scope: Estimation or critical-path scheduling
facts.objective: Validate the dependency graph and derive topological execution waves, refusing every malformed graph with a named finding rather than a guess.
facts.risk: Low
facts.why: A dependency list without validation is a suggestion. A cycle that nobody detects becomes a set of issues that can never be ready and nobody can explain why.

nodes.label: I0005
nodes.summary: Implement the plan command surface

acceptance_criteria: plan start refuses an issue that is not READY
plan done refuses while a required evidence token has no evidence
plan evidence refuses a token the issue does not require
plan evidence refuses without a command or an artifact
every subcommand answers --help and an unknown one exits 2
facts.current_state: The engine existed with no interface.
facts.desired_state: majordomus plan validate, status, list, show, ready, blocked, waves, graph, next, body, start, verify, evidence and done all read the one model.
non_scope: Any network call; the CLI never leaves the machine
facts.objective: Give a worker one command that answers what is ready, why something is blocked, what the graph looks like, and that moves an issue through its lifecycle while refusing illegal transitions.
facts.risk: Low
facts.why: A model nobody can query is a filing cabinet. The command is how a fresh session with no conversation history finds its work.

nodes.label: I0006
nodes.summary: Generate the Mermaid DAG from the graph

acceptance_criteria: Every node in the diagram is an issue in the model and every edge is a dependency in the model
Node styling reflects derived status
Restricting to one milestone emits only that milestone's subgraph
facts.current_state: The site rendered Mermaid for architecture diagrams written by hand in Markdown.
facts.desired_state: majordomus plan graph emits the DAG, and the docs, the site and the GitHub milestone body all use that output.
non_scope: Layout tuning beyond what Mermaid decides
facts.objective: Render the dependency graph as Mermaid from the same edges the engine derives, so that no diagram anywhere is drawn by hand.
facts.risk: Low
facts.why: A hand-drawn dependency diagram is a second source of truth that is wrong the first time an edge changes.

nodes.label: I0007
nodes.summary: Enforce the canonical model as doctrine

acceptance_criteria: A repository with no canonical model skips both doctrines rather than failing
An invalid model is a blocking doctor failure with a reproduce command
watch reports the same violations as drift
facts.current_state: The registry covered policy, profiles, scope, state, notes, projections and retention. Nothing covered the plan.
facts.desired_state: majordomus.project-integrity and majordomus.dag-integrity are declared, have validator functions, are dispatched by doctor and watch, and each has a test.
non_scope: Blocking a commit on a work-in-progress issue; progress is reported, not blocked
facts.objective: Add the project model to the doctrine registry so that doctor reports a broken model and watch reports a model that has drifted, through the same dispatcher every other rule uses.
facts.risk: A doctrine that fails in a repository without a project model would make every user installation red.
facts.why: A rule enforced by a script nobody runs is documentation. The doctrine registry is how this repository makes enforcement verifiable end to end.

nodes.label: I0008
nodes.summary: Project the model to GitHub milestones and issues

acceptance_criteria: The adapter runs offline against a fixture and produces the exact payload it would post
A managed issue whose body differs from the projection is reported as drift, not overwritten
A closed issue whose canonical status is not DONE is reported
The tool itself contains no network client
facts.current_state: The repository had no GitHub issues or milestones at all.
facts.desired_state: scripts/github-sync renders the projection from majordomus plan body, creates what is missing, updates what changed, and reports what a human has edited.
non_scope: Writing GitHub state back into the canonical files
Any network call inside bin, lib, share or test
facts.objective: Create and update GitHub milestones and issues from the canonical model, report drift instead of overwriting human edits, and keep every network call out of the tool itself.
facts.risk: A sync that overwrites a human comment thread would make GitHub hostile to use.
facts.why: GitHub is where collaboration happens, so it must show the plan. It is not where the plan lives, so it must never be the thing that defines it.

nodes.label: I0009
nodes.summary: Project the model into the website

acceptance_criteria: The generated data contains every milestone and issue with its derived status and wave
The roadmap, milestone, issue and DAG routes exist and are reachable from navigation
The pages are mobile-first and the DAG stays readable on a narrow screen
Stale generated data fails the sync check
facts.current_state: The site derived project, profiles, policy, claims, doctrines, commands and docs. It had no roadmap.
facts.desired_state: site/data/generated/plan.json exists, and the roadmap, milestone, issue and DAG routes render from it and from nothing else.
non_scope: Any hand-written roadmap content
facts.objective: Generate the roadmap, every milestone page, every issue page and the DAG page from the canonical model through the existing site data pipeline.
facts.risk: The site build is the slowest surface; a regression here is found late.
facts.why: The website already derives every capability claim from a canonical file. A hand-written roadmap page beside it would be the one page that can be wrong.

nodes.label: I0010
nodes.summary: Behavioural tests for schema, status, graph and command

acceptance_criteria: A duplicate id, an unknown dependency, a self-dependency and a cycle each have a negative case
READY, BLOCKED, ACTIVE, VERIFY and DONE each have a case
Wave assignment has a case with a diamond dependency
Every case runs in a disposable repository, never against this checkout
facts.current_state: No test touched the model.
facts.desired_state: Cases cover the schema, status derivation, the graph, the waves, the command surface and the doctrine wiring.
non_scope: Property-based testing frameworks
facts.objective: Prove each rule of the model with a case that fails when the rule is removed, in a disposable repository, the way every other rule here is proven.
facts.risk: Low
facts.why: The repository forbids a capability sentence without a test behind it. The model makes several capability sentences.

nodes.label: I0011
nodes.summary: Cross-surface consistency and mutation tests

acceptance_criteria: Canonical issue count equals CLI count equals site data count equals projection count
Canonical READY set equals the CLI READY set equals the site data READY set
Canonical edges equal Mermaid edges equal site data edges
Adding one dependency changes status, waves, Mermaid and site data together
facts.current_state: Each surface was tested on its own.
facts.desired_state: A case compares the issue set, the READY set and the edge set across surfaces, and a second case mutates a dependency and asserts every surface moved.
non_scope: Live GitHub calls in the test suite
facts.objective: Prove that the CLI, the generated site data and the GitHub projection describe the same graph, and that changing one canonical dependency changes all of them.
facts.risk: Low
facts.why: One engine is a claim. A test that compares the surfaces is the only thing that keeps it true after the next change.

nodes.label: I0012
nodes.summary: Make CI refuse an invalid model or a stale projection

acceptance_criteria: plan validate runs in the blocking job and its exit code is not swallowed
The GitHub projection is checked offline against the canonical model
No new step requires network access to succeed
facts.current_state: CI ran the suite, doctor, watch and the site data sync check.
facts.desired_state: CI also runs plan validate and the offline GitHub projection check, and fails on either.
non_scope: Any CI step that needs a GitHub token to pass
facts.objective: Add the model validation and the projection freshness check to the blocking CI job, with no advisory pass.
facts.risk: Low
facts.why: A validator that runs only when somebody remembers is not enforcement.

nodes.label: I0013
nodes.summary: Document the semantics and the dogfooding rule

acceptance_criteria: The documents explain semantics and contain no current-state figures
Every command they name exists and answers --help
Both appear on the website through the existing docs pipeline
facts.current_state: docs explained the task lifecycle and the doctrine chain, and nothing explained the plan.
facts.desired_state: docs/PLANNING.md explains the model and docs/DOGFOODING.md states the rule that Majordomus cannot recommend a discipline it does not use.
non_scope: Any count, progress figure or status written in prose
facts.objective: Write the human documentation that explains why the model exists and what its terms mean, and leave every current fact to be generated.
facts.risk: Low
facts.why: Documentation that states current state goes stale. Documentation that states semantics does not. The split has to be deliberate or the first roadmap paragraph rots.

nodes.label: I0014
nodes.summary: Make the worker instructions require the model

acceptance_criteria: The always-loaded projection instructs a worker to take work from plan next
The projection stays within the policy line budget
Regenerating the projections produces no diff
facts.current_state: The projection body described the task lifecycle and said nothing about milestones, issues or dependencies.
facts.desired_state: The generated CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md carry the plan lifecycle, and the projections stay inside their line budget.
non_scope: Provider-specific wording; the body is provider neutral
facts.objective: Change the always-loaded provider instructions so that a fresh worker of any provider selects work through the model rather than from conversation or a TODO list.
facts.risk: The always-loaded budget is a hard cap; adding text can push the projection over it.
facts.why: The model only becomes the way work happens if the file every worker loads first says so.

nodes.label: I0015
nodes.summary: Open the first real milestone and execute one issue through it

acceptance_criteria: The milestone addresses a defect or gap the repository already recorded, not one invented for this issue
One issue moved READY to ACTIVE to VERIFY to DONE through the command surface
The evidence attached to it is a command and its result, not a narrative
The next ready issue after it is derived, not chosen
facts.current_state: M000 was executed partly outside the system, because the system did not exist when it began.
facts.desired_state: A real post-bootstrap milestone exists, one of its issues is DONE with evidence recorded through plan evidence, and the graph has recomputed the next ready issue.
non_scope: A synthetic demonstration milestone
facts.objective: Prove the system on real repository work: open a milestone that exists because the repository needs it, and take one of its issues from READY to DONE entirely through the model.
facts.risk: Choosing a milestone to make the demonstration easy would defeat the purpose.
facts.why: Infrastructure that has never carried real work is a demo. The cutover is the only evidence that the discipline is usable.

nodes.label: I0101
nodes.summary: Reproduce the escaped blocker as an executable case

acceptance_criteria: The case opens a question against a task, hands over, starts a new task, and reaches a completed finish
It asserts the current outcome explicitly and says in a comment that this is the gap, not the goal
It runs in a disposable repository like every other case
facts.current_state: docs/CLAIMS.yaml says the blocker is escapable and cites no test. Nothing in test/cases exercises the sequence across a handover.
non_scope: Any change to lib/question.sh or lib/check.sh
facts.risk: A characterisation test pinning the wrong behaviour is a trap if nobody reads the comment. The comment is the whole safety mechanism, so it has to be unmissable.
facts.why: A defect described in prose is a defect nobody can prove was fixed. The case has to exist before the fix, or the fix has no witness.

nodes.label: I0102
nodes.summary: Decide whether a question transfers or the gate widens

acceptance_criteria: The decision names both alternatives and the case each one gets wrong
It cites the case from I0101 as its evidence
It is attributable to a task, which majordomus check verifies
facts.current_state: The claim note names the two alternatives and stops there. No decision record exists.
facts.desired_state: A dated entry in .majordomus/state/decisions.md names the choice, the rejected alternative, the case each is wrong in, and the evidence it rests on.
non_scope: Implementing the decision
facts.objective: Choose between the two alternatives the claim names, record the decision with what was rejected and why, and state which case the chosen behaviour is deliberately wrong in.
facts.risk: A decision recorded without the failing case behind it is an opinion.
facts.why: The claim was published as unfixed precisely because both answers are wrong somewhere. Implementing one without recording why is how a repository acquires behaviour nobody can defend.

nodes.label: I0103
nodes.summary: Implement the decision and prove it holds

acceptance_criteria: The case from I0101 asserts the chosen behaviour rather than the gap
Reverting the implementation turns that case red, demonstrated by running it against the reverted source
majordomus doctor and majordomus watch stay green
facts.current_state: The gate reads only unresolved questions belonging to the active task.
facts.desired_state: The behaviour the decision chose is implemented, and removing it turns a case red.
non_scope: Changing any other line of the finish contract
facts.objective: Make the chosen behaviour real in the question store and the blocker gate, and turn the characterisation case from I0101 into a case that fails when the behaviour is removed.
facts.risk: The question store's line format is machine-written and read by three commands; a change to it has to keep every existing entry parseable, which majordomus.questions-store-integrity checks.
facts.why: The gate is the only mechanism in the tool that stops a completed finish for a human reason. A gate with a known escape is worse than none, because people trust it.

nodes.label: I0104
nodes.summary: Move the claim from planned to guaranteed

acceptance_criteria: The claim is guaranteed and both paths exist
The detail page has a section saying what the behaviour does not cover
The generated site data regenerates without a stale file
facts.current_state: blocker-survives-handover is planned, with implementation and test both '-', and a note describing the gap.
facts.desired_state: The claim is guaranteed, cites lib/question.sh and the case from I0103, and its detail page says what the behaviour does not cover.
non_scope: Any behaviour change
facts.objective: Update docs/CLAIMS.yaml and the claim's detail page so the public surface states what is now true, with the file that implements it and the test that proves it.
facts.risk: Promoting a claim is the moment the repository starts being believed on it.
facts.why: A capability that works and is still published as planned understates the tool; one published as guaranteed without a test overstates it. The matrix is the only place either is caught.

nodes.label: I0201
nodes.summary: Declare which profile axis may become which runtime limit

acceptance_criteria: The mapping is one canonical file, read by the tool and written by hand nowhere else
Every declared axis exists on every profile, and an axis that does not is refused by name
A declared limit whose adapter does not exist is refused, and an adapter for an undeclared limit is refused
Every profile resolves to a complete set of limits, printed as data rather than prose
non_scope: Applying any limit; this issue only declares what may be applied
Any axis whose enforcement could not be observed from this repository
facts.risk: Declaring an axis enforceable before an adapter can apply it is how the previous attempt became theatre; the reconciliation in both directions is the guard against repeating it.

nodes.label: I0202
nodes.summary: Resolve a task's effective limits and print them as data

acceptance_criteria: The command prints every declared limit, its value, and the profile axis it was derived from
JSON output carries the same set the text output does
With no active task the default profile is resolved and named as the default
The resolver is the only place a limit value is computed
facts.current_state: The mapping declares what a limit is. Nothing computes the limits for a given task, and the task record carries no way to ask.
facts.desired_state: Running one command inside a task prints every limit the profile derives and the axis each came from. With no active task it resolves the default profile and says so.
non_scope: Enforcing any limit
Caching the resolved values anywhere; resolution is cheap and stays derived
facts.risk: A second computation of a limit anywhere else silently forks the contract; the case has to compare the enforced value against this command's output rather than against a constant.

nodes.label: I0203
nodes.summary: Make enforcement opt-in, and prove a repository that declines is unaffected

acceptance_criteria: The key is declared in the policy allowlist and rejected when it holds anything but a boolean
Default and absent both mean off, and the projections say so where a worker reads them
A case runs the full lifecycle in a repository that never sets the key and shows unchanged behaviour
Doctor reports whether enforcement is on, without turning it on
facts.current_state: Nothing is enforced, so nothing needs an opt-in. Adding the adapter without one would enforce limits in every repository that updates.
facts.desired_state: The policy carries an explicit enforcement key. Absent or false, the tool behaves as it did before the adapter existed, and a case demonstrates that rather than asserting it.
non_scope: Any default that enables enforcement
Per-command overrides; the choice is the repository's, once
facts.objective: Add one policy key that turns runtime enforcement on, default it to off, and prove with a case that a repository which never sets it behaves exactly as it does today.
facts.risk: An opt-in that defaults to on in the skeleton is not an opt-in; the skeleton has to be covered by the same case.

nodes.label: I0204
nodes.summary: Apply one derived limit for real and prove it changes what happens

acceptance_criteria: The applied value comes from the resolver, and no constant appears in the adapter
A case changes only the profile and observes a different outcome
A case with enforcement off observes the unconstrained outcome
Removing the application makes a case fail rather than a document go stale
facts.current_state: The mapping exists, the resolver prints the numbers, and the opt-in exists. Nothing anywhere applies a value to anything.
facts.desired_state: With enforcement on, one provider's execution is constrained by a value derived from the active profile, and turning the profile from one value to another changes the observed outcome.
non_scope: A second provider; one honest adapter first
Any provider knob whose effect cannot be observed from a test in this repository

nodes.label: I0205
nodes.summary: Declare the clamp as a doctrine so the mapping and the adapter cannot drift

acceptance_criteria: The doctrine is declared in the registry with its validator, and doctor fails if either half is missing
An adapter that applies a value the mapping does not derive is refused, and the refusal names the doctrine
A case covers the refusal and CI runs it
facts.current_state: One adapter applies one derived limit. Nothing refuses an adapter that stops consulting the mapping, and nothing lists this rule among the rules the repository enforces.
facts.desired_state: The rule appears in the doctrine list, a refusal names it, doctor proves it reaches its command and that a case covers it, and CI runs that case.
non_scope: Blocking on anything a worker cannot fix from inside the repository
facts.risk: A blocking doctrine over a provider-specific adapter can refuse work in a repository whose provider changed underneath it; whether it blocks or advises is decided against that, and recorded.

nodes.label: I0206
nodes.summary: Publish the runtime-adapters claim with the test that proves it and the limits it does not cover

acceptance_criteria: The claim cites an implementation path and a test path that both exist
The detail page names the axes that remain advisory
The generated site data regenerates with no stale file
facts.current_state: The claim is planned, with no implementation and no test, and its note describes the rolled-back attempt.
facts.desired_state: The claim is guaranteed for the limits that are actually applied, names the file and the case, and says plainly which axes are still advice.
non_scope: Any behaviour change
Widening the claim beyond the limits an adapter applies
facts.risk: This is the moment the repository starts being believed about runtime enforcement; a claim wider than the adapter is worse than no claim.
facts.why: A claim promoted to the width of its milestone title overstates what one adapter does. The matrix is where the difference between what is enforced and what is described is either kept honest or lost.

nodes.label: I0301
nodes.summary: Define the execution record, including what an absence looks like

acceptance_criteria: Every field names the reporter it came from, and a record without a reporter is refused
not_reported is representable with a reason, and is distinguishable from zero everywhere it is read
Unknown keys are refused like every other record in this repository
The schema is documented where the other file formats are
facts.current_state: Nothing measures a session. The economics document states what measurement would take and deliberately claims nothing, and no schema exists to be filled.
facts.desired_state: One schema, with an allowlist like every other record here, in which each measured field names its reporter, and not_reported is a first-class value carrying why it is absent.
non_scope: Collecting anything; this issue defines what would be stored
Any field the tool would have to estimate to populate
facts.risk: A schema designed around one provider's numbers becomes that provider's schema; the reporter field is what keeps a second provider from having to lie to fit.

nodes.label: I0302
nodes.summary: Record telemetry a provider reports, and refuse anything it did not

acceptance_criteria: Measured facts attach to the active task and survive into the completed record
A field without a reporter, or with a reporter that is not named, is refused
No code path fabricates, interpolates or defaults a measured value
The command works with no network and leaves no background process
facts.current_state: The record has a shape and nothing writes one.
facts.desired_state: A worker or a wrapper hands measured facts to one command, they are validated and stored against the task, and a value with no reporter is refused with a finding that names the field.
non_scope: Any network call, poll, or background collection
Deriving one field from another to fill a gap
facts.objective: Add the command that attaches measured execution facts to the active task, accepting only values a provider actually reported and refusing any field the caller cannot attribute to a reporter.
facts.risk: A provider's self-reported usage may itself be wrong; the record says who reported it so that a later correction has something to correct.
facts.why: The tool never invokes a model, so it cannot measure a session itself; the numbers have to be handed to it. The boundary where they arrive is the only place their provenance can still be checked.

nodes.label: I0303
nodes.summary: Prove a silent provider produces an explicit absence, never a guess

acceptance_criteria: The case runs start to finish with no telemetry reported and reaches a completed outcome
The stored record carries not_reported with a reason naming the provider
No surface prints a number for a task that reported none
facts.current_state: The recording path exists. What happens when nobody reports anything is untested.
facts.desired_state: A case demonstrates the silent path end to end, and a grep-like assertion over the reporting surfaces shows no estimated value is ever printed as measured.
non_scope: Any change to the recording path; if the case fails, the fix belongs to the issue that owns that code
facts.risk: A case that only checks the stored file misses a surface that fills a gap on its way to the screen; it has to assert on what is printed as well.

nodes.label: I0304
nodes.summary: Read the measurements back through the history surface, under a bound

acceptance_criteria: History shows measured facts and explicit absences for past tasks
The store has a declared retention bound and the bound is enforced by a case
No aggregate figure appears at this layer
facts.current_state: Facts are recorded against tasks and can be read only from the record itself.
facts.desired_state: History reports the measured facts alongside the task they belong to, says not_reported where that is what happened, and the store is capped like the ledger.
non_scope: Aggregation, averages or any figure derived across tasks; that is the next milestone
facts.objective: Make recorded execution facts readable through the surface that already answers questions about past tasks, with the same retention bound the other durable stores carry.
facts.risk: Showing per-task numbers invites reading a trend into them; the surface has to present facts without implying a series.

nodes.label: I0305
nodes.summary: Publish the telemetry claim and record what remains unmeasured

acceptance_criteria: The claim cites an implementation path and a test path that both exist
The economics document names the measured and unmeasured cases
The generated site data regenerates with no stale file
facts.current_state: The claim is planned and the economics document claims nothing on purpose.
facts.desired_state: The claim is guaranteed with its narrow scope stated, and the economics document says which providers are measured, which are not, and what follows from that.
non_scope: Any figure derived from the measurements
facts.risk: Publishing measurement invites treating partial coverage as full coverage; the coverage statement has to sit next to the claim, not in a footnote.

nodes.label: I0401
nodes.summary: Define an accepted outcome, and join it to its measurements without storing the join

acceptance_criteria: The definition matches what the finish contract enforces, and a case fails if the two drift apart
The join is derived from existing records, with nothing new persisted
An outcome whose work reported no telemetry appears in the set with an explicit absence
facts.current_state: The finish contract evaluates acceptance and records the outcome. Telemetry records what a session consumed. Nothing connects them, and the word outcome is used loosely across the documents.
non_scope: Any stored aggregate
Counting a completed finish that the contract did not accept
facts.risk: The tempting definition is the one that produces more data points; the correct one is the one the finish contract already enforces, even when that is a smaller set.

nodes.label: I0402
nodes.summary: Report cost only where measurement and acceptance both exist

acceptance_criteria: A figure is reported only where a measured record and an accepted outcome both exist
Where no figure is reported, the output names which half was missing
JSON and text agree on the set of outcomes and the figures reported
facts.current_state: The join exists as a derivation. Nothing reports it.
facts.desired_state: One command answers what an accepted outcome cost, in text and as JSON, and where it cannot answer, it names whether acceptance or measurement was missing.
non_scope: Elapsed time or token count used as a proxy for progress
Any projection of a future cost
facts.objective: Add the command that reports what accepted outcomes cost, computed only from measured facts, and reports no figure at all where either half is missing, saying which half.
facts.risk: The first number this command prints will be quoted somewhere; its units and its denominator have to be in the output itself, not only in the documentation.
facts.why: A cost report that fills gaps is worse than no cost report, because it is believed. The command has to be as willing to answer nothing as to answer a number.

nodes.label: I0403
nodes.summary: Make a thin denominator say so rather than average it away

acceptance_criteria: Every reported figure carries the count of accepted outcomes behind it
Below the declared threshold the output presents observations and no average
The threshold is declared as data, not written into the code path
Cases cover the thin case and the sufficient case
facts.current_state: The command reports figures from whatever measured, accepted outcomes exist, however few.
facts.desired_state: Each figure states its denominator, and below the threshold the output presents observations rather than a summary statistic.
non_scope: A confidence interval or any statistical model beyond stating the denominator
facts.objective: Make every reported figure carry the number of accepted outcomes it rests on, refuse to present a single observation as an average, and prove both with cases.
facts.risk: Any threshold is arbitrary; declaring it as data and printing it beside the figure is what keeps it honest rather than hidden.
facts.why: Early on there will be very few accepted outcomes, and a mean over one of them looks exactly like a mean over many. The report has to make the difference impossible to miss.

nodes.label: I0404
nodes.summary: Publish the cost-per-outcome claim with its unit defined beside it

acceptance_criteria: The claim cites an implementation path and a test path that both exist
The unit and denominator are defined where the figure is presented
The document states what the figure cannot be used to compare
The generated site data regenerates with no stale file
facts.current_state: The claim is planned. The economics document argues for the unit and reports nothing.
facts.desired_state: The claim is guaranteed, the unit and denominator are defined next to the reported figure, and the limits of comparison are stated.
non_scope: Any comparison against another tool or another team

facts.risk: A published cost figure is the most quotable thing this repository will produce and the most easily stripped of its qualifiers.
facts.why: Cost per accepted outcome is the one figure this project argues is the right unit. Publishing it without saying what it excludes would repeat the mistake the economics document was written to avoid.

nodes.label: I0501
nodes.summary: Group comparable work from what the records already carry

acceptance_criteria: Grouping uses only fields already recorded, and names them in its output
No new record type or vocabulary is introduced
Work that cannot be grouped is reported as ungrouped rather than forced into a group
facts.current_state: Records carry a profile, a declared scope, a verification result and an outcome. Nothing groups them, and nothing says what makes two tasks comparable.

non_scope: A hand-written taxonomy of task types
Any new noun; the grouping is a derivation, not a record

facts.risk: A grouping that is too coarse makes every recommendation the same one; too fine and no group ever reaches a usable denominator. Whichever is chosen has to be visible in the output.

nodes.label: I0502
nodes.summary: Recommend a profile from measured cost, naming the measurements

acceptance_criteria: Every recommendation lists the accepted outcomes and figures it was derived from
The recommendation names the group and how the group was derived
The command reads records and computes nothing that the cost layer already computes
facts.current_state: Cost per accepted outcome is reported per outcome. Nothing recommends anything.
facts.desired_state: Asking which profile a class of work should use returns a profile, the measurements behind it, and the group they came from.
non_scope: Invoking a model, or choosing a provider on a worker's behalf
facts.objective: Add the command that recommends a profile for a class of work from measured cost per accepted outcome, and prints the measurements the recommendation was derived from alongside it.
facts.risk: Following a recommendation produces the data that justifies it; the output has to record that the measurements postdate earlier recommendations.

nodes.label: I0503
nodes.summary: Return no recommendation where the data is too thin, and say why

acceptance_criteria: The threshold is declared as data and printed with every answer and every refusal
Below it, no profile is named at all
Cases cover both sides of the threshold
facts.current_state: The command recommends from whatever measurements exist.
facts.desired_state: Below the threshold the command returns no recommendation and names what it would take to have one; above it, the recommendation carries its denominator.
non_scope: A weaker recommendation with a caveat attached
facts.objective: Make insufficient data produce no recommendation rather than a weak one, with the threshold declared as data and the reason printed, proved by cases on both sides of it.
facts.risk: A threshold nobody can reach makes the whole command dead code; if the case shows the bar is unreachable in practice, that is a finding about the milestone, not a reason to lower it quietly.
facts.why: The failure mode of every routing feature is a confident answer from three data points. Refusing to answer is the behaviour that has to be tested, because it is the one that will be pressured away.

nodes.label: I0504
nodes.summary: Prove the recommendation is advisory and publish it as such

acceptance_criteria: A case shows a task starting under a profile different from the recommended one, unimpeded
The claim cites an implementation path and a test path that both exist and says recommendations only
The generated site data regenerates with no stale file
facts.current_state: The command answers with a profile and a basis. Nothing proves it cannot act on its own answer.
facts.desired_state: A case starts a task after a recommendation and shows the profile is whatever the worker asked for, and the claim says recommendations only.
non_scope: Any automatic application of a recommendation, behind a flag or otherwise
facts.objective: Prove with a case that a recommendation never changes the profile a task runs under, and publish the routing claim stating that Majordomus recommends and does not route.
facts.risk: A tool that recommends is one flag away from a tool that decides; the case is the record of the decision not to add the flag.

nodes.label: I0601
nodes.summary: Let a policy name a shared source it does not copy

acceptance_criteria: A shared source is resolved from the filesystem with no network access
Every policy reader sees the resolved policy, and no reader bypasses resolution
An unresolvable source is a named finding that stops the command, never a silent fallback to local
A repository that names no shared source behaves exactly as it does today
facts.current_state: Policy is per repository and entirely local. Nothing refers to anything outside the checkout.
facts.desired_state: A policy names a shared source, the tool resolves it without a network call, and every command that reads policy reads the resolved result.
non_scope: Fetching a policy over a network, from a registry, or from any service
A hosted component that must be running for the tool to work
facts.objective: Let a repository's policy name a shared policy source and resolve it offline from the filesystem, so that one statement of a rule can govern more than one repository without being pasted into each.
facts.risk: This is where a local-first tool grows a dependency outside its checkout; keeping resolution to the filesystem is what preserves the offline guarantee.

nodes.label: I0602
nodes.summary: Make a local override explicit and prove it survives an update of the shared source

acceptance_criteria: An override is a declaration, and a local value that differs without one is a finding
The merge order is documented and covered by a case
A case updates the shared source and shows the override still applies
facts.current_state: A shared source can be named and resolved. Anything a repository writes locally either wins or loses by a rule nobody has written down.
facts.desired_state: Overrides are declared, the merge order is documented and tested, and a shared source that changes underneath a repository does not silently take an override away.
non_scope: Overriding a rule the shared policy declares non-overridable, if such a class is introduced later
facts.risk: Merge semantics are where shared configuration usually becomes unexplainable; the documented order and its case are the whole defence.
facts.why: An override that looks like an ordinary key is indistinguishable from a stale copy. Declaring it is what lets the drift report tell a deliberate exception from an accident.

nodes.label: I0603
nodes.summary: Report drift from the shared policy in one command

acceptance_criteria: Every difference is listed with the key, both values, and whether it is declared
Undeclared divergence exits non-zero and declared overrides do not
Every finding carries a reproduce command
The command writes nothing

facts.desired_state: One command lists each difference, says whether it is a declared override or undeclared divergence, and names the reproduce command for each.
non_scope: Changing anybody's policy; the command reports and never writes
facts.objective: Report, in one command, every way a repository's effective policy differs from the shared source it names, separating declared overrides from undeclared divergence.
facts.risk: A drift report that is noisy is a drift report nobody runs; declared overrides have to be quiet by default.
facts.why: The point of naming a shared source is being able to see where it is not being followed. Without one command that answers that, shared policy is just a longer path to the same drift.

nodes.label: I0604
nodes.summary: Prove the offline guarantee survives sharing

acceptance_criteria: A doctrine declares the rule, its validator exists, and doctor proves it reaches the command that runs it
A case shows an unavailable shared source producing a named refusal, with nothing fetched and no fallback
CI runs the case
facts.current_state: Resolution, override and drift reporting all exist and are documented as filesystem-only. Nothing enforces that they stay so.
facts.desired_state: A doctrine refuses a network call in the policy resolution path, cases cover an unavailable source, and the refusal names the doctrine.
non_scope: Any offline cache of a remote source, which would be a fetch with extra steps

nodes.label: I0605
nodes.summary: Publish the shared-policy claim and what sharing still cannot do

acceptance_criteria: The claim cites an implementation path and a test path that both exist
The limitations page names what shared policy does not do
The design document no longer defers what has shipped, and still refuses what has not
The generated site data regenerates with no stale file

facts.desired_state: The claim is guaranteed for what is implemented, the limitations page names what it is not, and the design document's deferral is reconciled with what now exists.
non_scope: Any claim about repositories that have not adopted the shared source
facts.risk: This claim is the one a reader will most want to be wider than it is.
facts.why: Shared policy is the version most easily read as an organisational control plane. The claim has to name the boundary in the same place it names the capability, or the boundary will be assumed away.

nodes.label: I0701
nodes.summary: Reproduce the misattribution as an executable case

acceptance_criteria: The case starts a task, then records a decision as a second worker, and reaches an entry in decisions.md
It asserts the current attribution explicitly and marks it in a comment as the gap, not the goal

non_scope: Any change to lib/decision.sh, lib/checkpoint.sh or lib/question.sh
facts.risk: A characterisation test that pins the wrong behaviour is a trap unless the comment saying so is unmissable; that comment is the whole safety mechanism.

nodes.label: I0702
nodes.summary: Decide how a record is attributed, between named alternatives

acceptance_criteria: The record names the choice and both rejected alternatives, each with the case it gets wrong
Any identity the choice relies on is supplied by the session and stored only inside the record it explains
The conditions the implementation must meet are stated, not left to the implementer

facts.desired_state: One decision record naming the choice, both rejected alternatives, and the situation each of them is wrong in, with the conditions the choice imposes on the implementation.
non_scope: Implementing anything

nodes.label: I0703
nodes.summary: Implement the decision and prove it holds

acceptance_criteria: Every command that writes a durable record is covered, not only decision
The case from I0701 asserts the guarantee rather than the gap
A refusal names the rule and the command that resolves it
If the rule is enforced, it is declared in share/doctrines.yaml and doctor proves it reaches its command
facts.current_state: The choice is recorded. decision, checkpoint and question still resolve the active task from the checkout, and the case still asserts that.
non_scope: Any behaviour the decision did not choose
facts.objective: Implement whatever I0702 decided across every command that writes a durable record, and turn the characterisation case into one that asserts the new behaviour.
facts.risk: Three commands share this resolution path; fixing one and not the others leaves a defect that looks fixed, which is worse than one that looks broken.

nodes.label: I0704
nodes.summary: Publish what attribution guarantees, and what it still cannot

acceptance_criteria: The claim cites an implementation path and a test path that both exist
The detail page says the identity is supplied, not verified
The generated site data regenerates with no stale file

Any claim about verifying who a worker is

nodes.summary: Narrow the Clean Extraction Boundary and record what was adopted

Naming any internal path, component or vocabulary of the studied material

Any reading of the ledger
Knowledge

Retention and archiving
Any copying of a checkpoint, handover or decision body into the session file

A session from another branch is never offered as latest

Any repository-wide resolution across worktrees

nodes.label: I0806
nodes.summary: Make the session rules doctrines, with retention and archiving

A session naming a checkpoint path that does not exist is reported, naming both

Deleting a record under any circumstance

Any recursive walk of a hidden directory
Indexing a path merely because it exists

nodes.label: I0808
nodes.summary: Extract nodes with identities that survive a rebuild

acceptance_criteria: Two syncs of an unchanged repository produce byte-identical node output
Renaming a document changes that document's node id and no other
A node's kind comes from its source class or an explicit field, and a case proves prose containing a kind word does not change it
An unrecognisable source produces a node of kind unknown rather than being dropped or guessed at
Extraction from a generic Markdown document takes only the path, the first heading and explicit links

The manifest
Any full Markdown parser

nodes.label: I0809
nodes.summary: Record only edges that a file states, each with where it was observed

acceptance_criteria: Every edge carries the source file it was observed in, and an edge without provenance is a validation failure rather than a silent drop

Any similarity, clustering or taxonomy generation
Session edges, which arrive with the session integration

nodes.summary: A content-hash manifest that makes a second sync cheap

The measured cost of a no-op sync and of a cold sync on this repository is recorded as evidence

non_scope: Search
Any automatic rebuild triggered by a read

nodes.label: I0811
nodes.summary: Read-only knowledge lookup with an ordering that can be explained

Embeddings, similarity, or any opaque score
Rebuilding the index from a read

non_scope: Repairing anything automatically
Failing on a link to a resource outside the repository

nodes.label: I0813
nodes.summary: A closed session becomes a node that points at its episode

A high-volume record kind does not produce one node per file where a reference list is sufficient, and the reason is stated

non_scope: Any inference about why a session touched something
Copying a session summary into a node

nodes.label: I0814
nodes.summary: Give the worker a bounded slice of knowledge, not the knowledge base

The existing context case still passes unchanged

Rebuilding the index from context
Raising the existing line budget

nodes.summary: Say what is now true in the claims, the documentation and the worker instructions

The Clean Extraction Boundary and the continuity document agree with each other about the graph
The regenerated provider projections stay under the always-loaded budget
The instruction source teaches retrieval, not reading the whole base

A claim for a subcommand that has no behaviour of its own

The measurements are recorded, and no number appears in README or claims that they do not support
A read-only pass over the whole surface leaves git status byte-identical

Any performance guarantee in README or claims that the measurement does not support

Off, a phase or a count costs one test and no subprocess

Timing that is on when MJ_TIMING is unset

nodes.label: I0818
nodes.summary: The command registry is read in one pass

Cases 30, 31, 35 and 36 pass unchanged

nodes.summary: The project model is loaded with one flatten per file and no per-file lookups

Cases 40 to 48 pass unchanged

The cases that mutate their inputs still fail on the mutation

nodes.summary: Every canonical file is flattened at most once per command

facts.risk: The served topology is in flight on other branches. Pinning the suite to today's paths would make it stale on arrival; it has to ask the topology rather than name arms.

nodes.label: I0917
nodes.summary: A bad deployment can be undone deterministically

acceptance_criteria: The previously deployed image reference is captured before the deployment mutates anything
A failed post-deployment smoke run fails the deployment clearly and reports the new and previous references without exposing a credential
The rollback path rests on the provider's documented current behaviour, and is either executed automatically because it has been proved to work or offered as one deterministic command
The rollback is documented where an operator under pressure will find it
facts.current_state: Nothing is deployed and nothing records what was deployed before.
facts.desired_state: The previous image reference is captured before every deploy, a failed smoke run reports both references safely, and one documented command returns production to the previous image.
non_scope: Inventing a provider command that does not exist
Automatic rollback that has never been executed successfully in a test
facts.objective: Record the deployed image reference before changing production and provide a rollback that rests on what the provider actually supports, so that a failed smoke run has an exit.
facts.risk: An automatic rollback that has never run is a second failure mode during the first real incident. Either it is tested or it is a documented manual command.
facts.why: Autostop and a single machine mean a bad image is the only image. Knowing the previous reference before the change is what makes recovery a command instead of an investigation.

nodes.label: I0918
nodes.summary: The bootstrap credential is used once and belongs to nothing

acceptance_criteria: The discovery order is documented and implemented — an existing environment variable, then an already authenticated provider CLI, and nothing that reads another repository
Credential validity is confirmed with a command that returns an identity and never a secret
No token value can be printed by any code path, including verbose output, error messages and traces
A check proves no path belonging to another repository appears anywhere in this one
Deployment credentials and application runtime secrets are treated as distinct concepts, and the distinction is documented
facts.current_state: No deployment exists and no credential handling exists. A usable credential is expected to be reachable through the operator's existing authenticated tooling.
facts.desired_state: A documented discovery order finds an existing authenticated session, the token is consumed only in the current process, and no file in this repository names the external environment it came from.
non_scope: Any reference, in code, script, documentation, CI, test, default or generated artifact, to another repository's path or environment
Writing a token to any file in this repository
Passing a token as a build argument or baking it into an image layer
facts.objective: Define and implement how a deployment credential is discovered for an interactive first deployment, so that it is consumed in one process, never persisted, and leaves no trace of where it came from.
facts.risk: A convenience that reads the operator's other environment is exactly the dependency this issue exists to prevent. Bootstrap happens in a person's shell, not in this repository's code.

nodes.label: I0919
nodes.summary: Nothing secret and nothing local leaves in the image

acceptance_criteria: The image, its layer history and its environment are inspected, and the extracted filesystem too where that is feasible
The generated artifacts, the site output, the API document and the deployment report are inspected
Known credential variable names and credential-shaped values are both detected
Absolute developer paths are detected as their own class of finding
A finding names the location and the kind and never the value, and the check runs in CI
facts.current_state: No image exists and no scan exists.
facts.desired_state: A check inspects the image, its history and environment, the generated files and the published output, reports what it found by location and kind, and never prints a secret value.
non_scope: Printing any secret value, in any output, for any reason
A general-purpose secret scanner competing with existing repository tooling
facts.objective: Automate the verification that no credential material and no developer path appears in the image, its metadata, the generated artifacts, the site output, the API documents or the deployment report.
facts.risk: A scan that never fires is indistinguishable from a scan that cannot fire. It needs a negative test that plants a synthetic marker and proves the check finds it.
facts.why: Every one of those surfaces has published a secret for somebody at some point. A scan that runs in CI is the only version of this promise that stays true.

nodes.label: I0920
nodes.summary: The image's dependencies are known and its advisories are policy

acceptance_criteria: The runtime package inventory of the image is obtained and recorded
A dependency audit runs and its verdict is part of the gate
The severity and fix-availability policy is declared as data, not as prose, and the gate reads it
Where the repository's practice supports it, a bill of materials is produced alongside the image
External workflow actions are pinned to immutable references according to the repository's convention
facts.current_state: No image, no inventory, no scan and no policy exist.
facts.desired_state: The package inventory and the dependency audit are obtained by the same verification that runs everything else, and the policy states which findings block and which are recorded.
non_scope: A security dashboard or a vulnerability database of our own
Failing the build on advisories with no available fix and no exploitable path
facts.risk: A policy that blocks on everything is a policy nobody keeps. The threshold has to be stated where it can be reviewed rather than buried in a workflow.
facts.why: An image of unknown contents cannot be reasoned about after a disclosure. A scanner wired to fail on every advisory in every database is turned off within a week, which is worse than no scanner.

nodes.label: I0921
nodes.summary: Size is measured first and budgeted second

acceptance_criteria: Binary bytes, generated asset bytes, image size, compressed size where obtainable and the layer breakdown are all measured and recorded
The budgets are declared with stated headroom over the measured baseline and live as policy data
CI fails on growth beyond the budget and names what grew
The documentation and the UI read the baseline and the budget from the recorded data rather than from prose
facts.current_state: Nothing is measured because nothing is built.
non_scope: An arbitrary size target chosen before the first build
A second place where a size number is written by hand
facts.objective: Measure the binary, the assets, the image and the build context, declare budgets with headroom over the measured baseline, and gate unexplained growth.
facts.risk: A budget with no headroom fails on an unrelated dependency bump and trains everybody to raise it without looking.
facts.why: A budget invented before a measurement is a number somebody will disable. A budget derived from a measured baseline with stated headroom is a regression detector.

nodes.label: I0922
nodes.summary: The memory hypothesis is tested, not asserted

acceptance_criteria: The image runs under the declared limit and stays alive through the whole representative sequence
Resident memory is measured after startup and after a landing, documentation, API, OpenAPI and cockpit request, and the high-water mark is recorded
If the declared limit does not hold, the cause is diagnosed and the waste addressed before the limit is raised, and the raise is recorded with its evidence
The measurement is recorded through the existing benchmark infrastructure and becomes a regression budget
facts.current_state: The canonical object states a memory hypothesis. Nothing has been run under any limit.
facts.desired_state: Resident memory is measured at startup and after each representative request, the high-water mark is recorded, and the declared memory is the smallest value the evidence supports.
non_scope: Raising the limit before diagnosing what consumed the memory
A load test; this is a resource envelope, not a throughput study
facts.objective: Run the production image under the intended memory limit, measure resident memory through a representative request sequence, and let the evidence decide the memory the deployment declares.
facts.risk: A single machine's measurement is not a guarantee on another host. The high-water mark needs headroom, and the headroom needs to be stated.

nodes.label: I0923
nodes.summary: Cold start and endpoint cost are benchmark targets like everything else

acceptance_criteria: Process start to listening, process start to readiness and container start to readiness are each measured separately
The cheap endpoints are benchmarked under the constrained resource profile with distributions rather than a single number
The measurements are recorded as artifacts through the existing benchmark infrastructure with the environment they were taken on
No cold-start guarantee is stated that the repeatability of the measurement does not support
facts.current_state: The benchmark command derives its targets from the command registry and holds a committed baseline. Nothing measures a container or an HTTP endpoint under deployment conditions.
non_scope: A load-testing framework
A throughput claim derived from one machine
Promising a cold-start guarantee from an unrepeatable measurement
facts.objective: Measure the cold start of the container and the cost of the cheap endpoints through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has, and record them as baselines.
facts.risk: Container timings on a laptop and on a hosted machine differ enough that one cannot be a baseline for the other. The environment is part of the record.
facts.why: A profile with no minimum running machines means every idle period ends with a cold start that a user pays for. A number nobody measured cannot be improved and cannot be defended.

nodes.label: I0924
nodes.summary: The decision is recorded where architecture decisions are recorded

facts.desired_state: One ADR states the decision, the alternatives, the tradeoffs and what would have to change to revisit them, in the repository's own ADR format.
non_scope: A second ADR format or an ADR that restates the documentation
facts.objective: Write the architecture decision record for deploying as a generated projection of canonical deployment metadata, with the alternatives that were genuinely considered and the consequences that follow.
facts.risk: An ADR written after everything is finished records the implementation rather than the decision. It has to be written when the choice is still visible.

nodes.label: I0925
nodes.summary: Every deployment rule is a check that runs

acceptance_criteria: Deployment configuration originates from the canonical object, and editing a generated provider artifact by hand is refused by a check
Generated deployment artifacts must match the canonical object, and CI fails on drift
Secrets must not enter generated artifacts, source control, build arguments, layers, documentation or the UI, and a check enforces it
The production runtime image must contain only runtime dependencies and must run non-root, and a check enforces both
Deployment documentation and UI must derive from the authoritative data, and a check enforces it
A deployment must expose and test the canonical health and readiness behaviour, and a check enforces it
The declared cost profile must stay resource-bounded, and a change to the envelope is visible in review because a check names it
Each rule reuses an existing rule where one already covers the constraint rather than adding a near-duplicate
facts.current_state: Project rules exist for benchmarkable commands, derived files, hot paths, scope declaration, shared-server resilience and more, each with a check. None concerns deployment.
facts.desired_state: Each deployment rule exists as a rule object with a check that executes, and a violation is refused rather than reported in a document nobody reads.
non_scope: A rule with no executable check
Restating an existing rule that already covers the constraint
facts.objective: State the durable deployment constraints as project rules in the repository's rule system, and give each one an executable check that CI runs.
facts.risk: Seven new rules is a lot of doctrine for one subsystem. Any constraint an existing rule already covers should be referenced rather than restated.

nodes.label: I0926
nodes.summary: The deployment documentation is generated and reachable

facts.current_state: The site is generated from the registry and the documentation index. No deployment page exists and no navigation entry points at one.
non_scope: Deployment values retyped into prose
A hand-written navigation entry or landing card
Currency prices stated as permanent facts
facts.risk: Troubleshooting written before anything has failed is fiction. It is filled from the failures the implementation actually hits.

nodes.label: I0927
nodes.summary: The cockpit shows the deployment from the same data

acceptance_criteria: Static deployment policy comes from the canonical object and live facts from the same metadata read the API serves
No credential of any kind reaches the client, and a test proves it
The view carries no mutating control
The view appears through the cockpit's existing navigation derivation rather than a hardcoded entry
Absent live data renders as absent rather than as a broken or empty card
facts.current_state: The cockpit renders pages, navigation and views derived from the registry and the index, under ADR 0012, and is under active development on another branch.
non_scope: A second frontend, a second design language or a second data source
Any credential reaching the browser
Mutating deployment controls
facts.objective: Add a deployment view to the existing cockpit that reads static policy from the canonical object and live facts from the running process, using the projection the cockpit already is.
facts.risk: The cockpit is being rebuilt on another branch. This view has to be written against its projection model rather than against its current markup, and landed after it.

nodes.label: I0928
nodes.summary: A pull request cannot merge a deployment that would not work

facts.current_state: Two workflows exist: validation and pages. Neither knows anything about a deployment.
facts.desired_state: One gate covers the deployment checks alongside everything else, uses the existing caching, and never deploys from a pull request.
non_scope: A second overlapping workflow file
Deploying to production from a pull request
facts.risk: A gate that takes an hour is a gate people bypass. The container build has to be cached well enough that the added time is proportionate.
facts.why: The gate is where these checks stop being optional. Adding a separate workflow for deployment would fragment a verification story the repository has already unified once.

nodes.label: I0929
nodes.summary: Production deploys from CI with a token scoped to one application

acceptance_criteria: The deployment token is scoped to the application, has a deliberate expiry and a descriptive name
The token is installed as a repository secret without being echoed, printed or written to any file, or the exact one-time command is provided instead when that cannot be done safely
The workflow deploys through the same deployment core the CLI uses, with no second build implementation
Concurrency is configured deliberately so two pushes cannot deploy the same application at once, and the choice about cancellation is stated
External actions are pinned and the provider tool version is deliberate rather than floating
facts.current_state: No deployment workflow exists and no token has been created.
facts.desired_state: The production workflow deploys through the same core the CLI uses, holds only a scoped token, serialises deployments, and its token is installed without ever appearing in a log or a file.
non_scope: An account-wide token in CI
A CI-only container build implementation separate from the canonical one
Weakening the token model because a tool was unavailable
facts.risk: Cancelling an in-progress deployment can leave a machine half-updated. Whether cancellation is safe is a decision to make explicitly, not a default to inherit.

nodes.label: I0930
nodes.summary: The real image runs under the real limits before anything is deployed

acceptance_criteria: The image under test is the production image, built by the canonical build
It runs under the declared memory and CPU limits of the cheap profile, and with a read-only filesystem where the application permits it
The process stays alive, its user id is not zero, and it listens on the declared port
Liveness and readiness answer, and the landing, documentation, API document and static assets are served
Readiness is reached by bounded polling on an ephemeral port, with no sleep and no fixed port
facts.current_state: No image and no container test exist.
facts.desired_state: One test builds the production image, runs it constrained, polls readiness with a bounded timeout, and asserts the behaviour the deployment depends on.
non_scope: A fixed host port
A sleep standing in for readiness
A test image that differs from the production one
facts.objective: Build the actual production image and run it under the resource limits of the cheap profile, verifying the process, its user, its port and its routes without fixed ports and without sleeping.
facts.risk: A container test needs a container runtime, which not every environment has. It must skip explicitly and visibly where the runtime is absent rather than passing quietly.

nodes.label: I0931
nodes.summary: The application exists, one machine runs it, and the URL answers

facts.current_state: No application exists at any provider.
facts.desired_state: One application, one machine, the declared resources, the declared region, a public HTTPS URL that answers, a smoke suite that passes against it, and a machine-readable report of what was deployed.
non_scope: Creating a new application on any subsequent deploy
Mutating or deleting any unrelated application
Accepting a deploy command's exit code as verification
facts.risk: This is the issue that spends money and touches a real account. It runs once the container evidence is in, and the inventory assertion is what keeps a mistake from billing indefinitely.
facts.why: Everything before this is preparation. A deployment that has never run is a hypothesis, and an exit code from a deploy command is not evidence that anything is being served.

nodes.label: I0932
nodes.summary: The milestone is accepted on its evidence

acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of the milestone has evidence recorded against it
The measured baselines — binary, image, context, build durations, readiness, resident memory, endpoint latency — are documented with the machine and environment they were measured on
The developer workflow in the documentation runs exactly as written on a clean checkout
Pre-existing failures, failures introduced here and failures fixed here are distinguished explicitly
Remaining limitations are stated rather than omitted
facts.current_state: Open.
facts.desired_state: The milestone is accepted with evidence against every criterion, and the baselines and limitations are written where they will be found.
non_scope: Reporting a plan as an implementation
Recording a measurement without the environment it was taken on
facts.risk: The temptation at the end is to record intent as outcome. Anything not demonstrated is a limitation, and it is written as one.
facts.why: A milestone is accepted by its evidence. The numbers, the commands and the deployed URL are what a later reader has; this session's messages are not.

nodes.label: I1001
nodes.summary: One typed graph composes the registries that already own their facts

acceptance_criteria: Node kinds come from the kinds the layer already registers, and adding a kind does not require a new variant hand-written in the graph
Every source is read through the registry that owns it, never by a second traversal of the filesystem
Generation over identical repository contents produces structurally identical output, with no iteration-order dependence, no random identity and no timestamp inside the canonical data
The model separates a capability's definition from its runtime state, so that the static projection needs no runtime fields
Unit tests cover discovery, normalisation, deduplication and ordering
facts.current_state: graph.rs derives rule dependencies, decisions and the shape of the layer for the Cockpit and the site. The capability registry knows capabilities. Nothing joins the two, and no node type spans both.
facts.desired_state: One typed model holds nodes of every kind the repository already indexes, built by reading the registries through the paths every other caller uses, and producing the same output for the same inputs.
non_scope: A new store of anything an existing registry already owns
Reading the index outside the executor, the cache and the counters that every other read passes through
Node kinds invented here rather than taken from the kinds the layer already registers
facts.risk: Composing everything invites a model that knows too much and is slower than the hot path allows. It is built on the reads that already happen, and its cost is measured like every other command's.

nodes.label: I1002
nodes.summary: Relations are typed, inferred from stable identities, and never dangle

acceptance_criteria: Each relation type is explicit, and the direction is part of its meaning
Inference uses stable identities only, and an ambiguous case requires an explicit declaration instead of a guess
A relation whose target does not exist fails generation, naming where it was declared and what is missing
Tests cover malformed metadata, duplicate identities and dangling relations
facts.current_state: Relations exist implicitly in frontmatter references, capability tags, rule metadata and ADR related lists. Nothing resolves them into a common edge type, and nothing fails when one does not resolve.
facts.desired_state: Every edge has a type, both ends resolve to a node, and an unresolvable edge fails generation with a message naming the declaration, the missing end and the correction.
non_scope: Inference by substring or title matching where a stable identity exists
Requiring a contributor to restate a relation the metadata already implies
facts.risk: Strict resolution can make an unrelated documentation edit fail the build. The message has to be good enough that the failure is a five-second fix rather than an investigation.

nodes.label: I1003
nodes.summary: Skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases and benchmarks enter the graph as themselves

acceptance_criteria: Each kind is projected from its own registry with the metadata that registry holds, and no field is invented here
A rule shows what it governs, how it is enforced and what tests it; a skill shows its purpose, scope and relations; a decision shows what it puts in force
Adding a valid object under a canonical directory makes it appear in the graph with no further registration
Where a relation needs declaring, the field is added to the kind's existing schema rather than to a new one
facts.current_state: Each kind is indexed and readable as an object. The site renders some of them as lists. None is related to a capability by anything a machine reads.
facts.desired_state: Each kind is a node with the metadata its own registry holds, related to what it governs, documents, enforces, tests or measures.
non_scope: A second registry for any of these kinds
