Frontmatter conventions that conflict with the schemas those directories already define
facts.risk: Every kind has its own vocabulary, and flattening them into one node type loses what makes each useful. The node carries the kind's own metadata rather than a lowest common denominator.

nodes.label: I1004
nodes.summary: Availability and visibility are metadata, not conditions in a template

acceptance_criteria: Availability distinguishes at least what is always true, what requires the running backend, what is a build-time snapshot and what requires authentication
Visibility distinguishes public and developer-facing capabilities from ones deliberately marked internal
Every existing capability, route and surface is classified, and an unclassified one is a validation failure rather than a default
No projection decides availability from anything other than this metadata
facts.current_state: The Cockpit is served by the running process. The site is generated. Nothing states which capability means anything in which environment.
facts.desired_state: Availability and visibility are fields of the model, every projection reads them, and no template decides for itself.
non_scope: Any decision made from a hostname, a URL or a build-time flag inside a template
An internal capability being silently invisible without saying it is internal
facts.risk: A default of always-available makes the model useless and the classification invisible. Absence has to be a failure.

nodes.label: I1005
nodes.summary: The graph is a generated artifact with a schema and no unsafe field

acceptance_criteria: The artifact is produced by the existing generation target set, not by a separate script
It has a schema, and the schema is generated from the types rather than written by hand
Ordering is deterministic and repeated generation is byte-identical over identical inputs
It contains no credential, no private environment value and no machine-absolute path, proved by a test
Provenance is recorded in the artifact's own metadata where its format cannot carry a comment
facts.current_state: No aggregate artifact exists. The site reads several derived datasets, each from its own script.
facts.desired_state: One generated artifact carries the graph, with a schema, deterministic ordering, provenance and no field that must not be published.
non_scope: A hand-edited copy of the artifact
Any token, key, header, environment dump or machine-absolute path in the output
A timestamp inside the canonical data
facts.objective: Serialise the graph as a deterministic generated artifact with a schema, carrying safe metadata only, produced by the generation the repository already runs.
facts.risk: One artifact for everything grows until it is downloaded on every page load. Its size is measured and budgeted with the other assets.
facts.why: Both projections and every test need one file to read. Making it generated keeps it honest; giving it a schema makes it consumable; keeping it free of anything private makes it publishable.

nodes.label: I1006
nodes.summary: The runtime reads the graph through the registry, like every other read

acceptance_criteria: The operation is one capability declaration and appears in the API, the OpenAPI document, the reference and the benchmark coverage without a second registration
The response is typed and carries safe fields only
Runtime state is an overlay over the definitions, distinguishable in the response
A test exercises the operation against a running server rather than a mock
facts.current_state: The Cockpit renders in-process. No capability serves the aggregate graph.
facts.desired_state: One declared capability serves the graph, documented and benchmarked like the rest, with the runtime state layered over the definitions rather than mixed into them.
non_scope: A route registered outside the capability registry
Runtime state stored in the same structure as the definitions
facts.objective: Expose the graph to the running Cockpit as a declared capability, so that its route, its schema, its documentation and its benchmark coverage all follow from the declaration.
facts.risk: Serving the whole graph on every Cockpit load is a cost on the hot path. It is measured, and paged or filtered if the measurement says so.
facts.why: A route added by hand for the Cockpit would be the one endpoint missing from OpenAPI, from the reference and from the smoke suite. The registry exists precisely so that does not happen.

nodes.label: I1007
nodes.summary: The site renders the same graph, generated once

acceptance_criteria: The static projection is produced by the canonical generation target set, with any shell involved being a thin adapter
The published pages render the capabilities, the kinds, the relations and the coverage without any request to a backend
Build-time and runtime data are distinguishable on the page, and a captured measurement is labelled as captured rather than shown as current
The drift check covers the static projection
facts.current_state: The site is generated from the registry and several derived datasets by scripts that each know their own output.
facts.desired_state: The static projection is a target of the canonical generation, and the site consumes it like its other derived data.
non_scope: A standalone cockpit generation script
The static build requiring any runtime API to render
facts.risk: Rendering yesterday's health as though it were current is the failure mode this issue exists to prevent, and it is a labelling problem, not a data problem.
facts.why: A separate generation script for the site is the second universe this repository has already refused once. The generation target set exists and owns this.

nodes.label: I1008
nodes.summary: The two projections are proved to be the same model

acceptance_criteria: The comparison is over the normalised model, not over HTML
Runtime-only fields are removed by an explicit list that the test owns, so adding one to either side without declaring it fails
The test runs in CI on every change
facts.current_state: Only one projection exists today, so there is nothing to compare.
facts.desired_state: One test builds both, strips the runtime-only fields and asserts equality, and it fails when either projection grows a field the other does not know about.
non_scope: Asserting equality of rendered markup rather than of the model
facts.objective: Test that the static and runtime representations of the graph are equal once runtime-only fields are removed, so the published site and the running server cannot become alternate realities.
facts.risk: A parity test that strips too much passes trivially. The stripped list is small, explicit and reviewed.
facts.why: Two renderings of one model diverge silently, and the divergence is discovered by a person who trusted the wrong one. A parity test is the only thing that keeps them honest.

nodes.label: I1009
nodes.summary: Every menu in this repository comes from one derivation

acceptance_criteria: Every navigation surface reads the same projection, and none holds its own list
Grouping derives from metadata the model already carries, and ordering is deterministic and stable across builds
Adding a capability or a document changes every menu that should show it with no template edit
An entry unavailable in the current environment is not rendered as an active destination
facts.current_state: Navigation and landing content are assembled per surface. The landing page and the Cockpit each know their own entries.
facts.desired_state: One navigation projection feeds every surface, grouping derives from kind, category, scope and availability, and ordering is deterministic.
non_scope: Any hand-written menu entry in a template, a script or a data file
Layout coordinates, columns or component trees expressed as data
facts.why: Five menus mean five edits for one new page, and the fifth is the one everybody forgets. Grouping by facts the model already holds gives an order that is stable without anyone maintaining it.

nodes.label: I1010
nodes.summary: The overview is what exists, counted rather than claimed

acceptance_criteria: Sections are present only when the corresponding kind has members
Every number shown is computed from the graph at build or request time
A kind added to the layer appears in the overview with no change to the overview's own code
The counts on the page match the artifact, proved by a test
facts.current_state: The Cockpit renders pages derived from the registry and the index. Section presence and any counts are decided in code.
facts.desired_state: Sections appear because their kind has members, counts are computed, and a new kind of thing appears without the overview being rewritten.
non_scope: A number typed by a human anywhere in the interface
A heading rendered for a kind with no members
facts.objective: Generate the Cockpit overview and its summary numbers from the graph, showing a section only when the repository actually holds that kind of thing.
facts.risk: Counts on a page are the sort of thing the repository's own rule against numbers in prose exists for. They are computed and rendered, never written.
facts.why: A dashboard with headings for things that do not exist teaches readers to distrust it, and hand-maintained counts are wrong within a week. Both problems disappear when the overview is a query.

nodes.label: I1011
nodes.summary: The coverage matrix reports evidence, and never a green cell without one

acceptance_criteria: Every filled cell names the artifact that supports it and can be followed to it
A relation that claims evidence but does not resolve is reported as a gap, and the report says which end failed
The policy for what evidence a kind requires is data, not a condition in the renderer, and a descriptive kind is not asked for a behavioural test
The matrix is available in both projections and in machine-readable form
facts.current_state: Benchmark coverage exists for capabilities. Documentation, tests and enforcement have no coverage view at all.
facts.desired_state: Each cell resolves to a named artifact — a document, a test, a rule, a benchmark case — and an unresolved claim is reported as missing rather than shown as satisfied.
non_scope: A status a contributor can declare without an artifact behind it
Demanding evidence from purely descriptive metadata that has no behaviour to test
facts.objective: Generate a matrix showing, for every capability, whether it is documented, tested, enforced, benchmarked and exposed, where each cell resolves to an artifact or a relation rather than to a claim.
facts.risk: A matrix that is mostly empty on the first run will be read as an indictment rather than a baseline. It is a starting measurement, and saying so is part of shipping it.

nodes.label: I1012
nodes.summary: One detail view, assembled from what a node actually has

acceptance_criteria: Empty sections are absent rather than rendered blank
The deep link is built from the stable identity and survives a title change
Source references are repository-relative and never machine-absolute
The static projection produces compatible links
facts.current_state: The Cockpit renders views over the registry. Deep links and source traceability are not part of the model.
facts.desired_state: One assembly renders any node, showing only populated sections, with a stable link and a repository-relative source reference.
non_scope: A separate hardcoded template per kind unless the presentation genuinely differs
A machine-absolute path in any published output
Identity derived from a display title
facts.objective: Render a capability's detail page from its populated sections and its resolved relations, with a stable deep link and a repository-relative reference to where the information came from.
facts.risk: Traceability that publishes a path from the machine that built the site is a leak. Repository-relative is the only form that ships.

nodes.label: I1013
nodes.summary: Search over the graph, generated, with nothing to run

acceptance_criteria: The index is generated from the graph and covers identities, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, commands, routes and documents
Search works in the static build with no backend
A newly registered capability is findable after generation with no further edit
The index size is measured and counted against the asset budget
facts.current_state: No unified search exists over the layer.
facts.desired_state: One generated index serves both projections, its contents derive from the graph, and it costs nothing to operate.
non_scope: An external search service for a graph of this size
A hand-maintained index or keyword list
facts.objective: Provide one search over identities, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, commands, routes and documents, from a generated index that works in the static build with no service behind it.
facts.risk: A client-side index grows with the repository until it dominates the page weight. Measuring it now is what makes the later decision to page or trim it a measurement rather than a surprise.
facts.why: A repository this size does not need a search service, and adding one would put the published site behind an availability dependency it currently does not have.

nodes.label: I1014
nodes.summary: The relation view reads the graph and holds no data of its own

acceptance_criteria: Every node and edge comes from the generated data
Filters operate on the model's fields — kind, category, source, surface, availability, relation type and the evidence flags
Zoom, pan, selection, neighbour highlighting, a detail panel and deep links all work, and a selected node resolves to its detail view
The library is lazily loaded and absent from pages without a graph
A textual equivalent of the same relations is available for anyone who cannot use the graph
Initialisation cost on this repository's data is measured
facts.current_state: The layer's graphs are derived and rendered for the site. There is no interactive relation view over the composed model.
facts.desired_state: One view reads the artifact, filters by the model's own fields, and is not loaded by pages that do not use it.
non_scope: Nodes or edges written into JavaScript
A visualisation library loaded on pages that do not render a graph
A three-dimensional rendering that replaces rather than supplements the accessible information
facts.objective: Render the relation graph interactively from the generated data, with filters, focus, neighbour highlighting and deep links, loaded only where it is used and bounded in cost.
facts.risk: Rendering every node at once is slow and unreadable at the same time. The default view is filtered, and expansion is progressive.
facts.why: The edges are the reason the model exists, and a static list cannot show them. But a visualisation with nodes written into a script is a second inventory in the least maintainable place available.

nodes.label: I1015
nodes.summary: A surface with no server behind it is not offered as if it had one

acceptance_criteria: A backend-only surface is offered as usable only where a backend is available, decided from metadata
The static build contains no active link to a runtime-only surface
Where mentioning an unavailable surface is useful, it is shown as unavailable rather than omitted silently or linked
Both cases are tested — the static build and a running server with the API present
facts.current_state: The Swagger shell and the API are served by the running process. The published site has no way to know that.
facts.desired_state: Exposure follows from availability metadata alone, and there is a test for each projection that keeps it that way.
non_scope: Any decision made from a hostname, an address or a build flag inside a page
Rendering a dead destination as if it were live
facts.objective: Make the exposure of backend-only surfaces — the API console, live status, runtime reads — follow from availability metadata, and prove both projections behave correctly.
facts.risk: This is the check that quietly rots, because a broken link on a published page fails nothing. The test for it has to run on every build.
facts.why: The published site has no server. A link to a runtime console on it is a broken promise, and the usual fix is a check on the page's own address, which is a rule hidden where nobody will find it.

nodes.label: I1016
nodes.summary: The Cockpit works on a phone and before JavaScript runs

acceptance_criteria: Navigation, content, tables and details are usable at narrow phone widths through to a wide desktop, with no horizontal page overflow at any of them
Touch targets are usable and focus is visible
The markup is semantic, keyboard navigation works, and status is never conveyed by colour alone
Core information is present in the served HTML before enhancement
facts.current_state: The Cockpit is server-rendered with its own stylesheet, and its behaviour across viewports has not been established for this material.
facts.desired_state: Navigation, cards, tables, details and the graph's textual equivalent are usable from a narrow phone width upward, nothing overflows horizontally, and the core content is in the HTML.
non_scope: Hiding content below a breakpoint instead of adapting it
Requiring JavaScript to discover a documentation link
facts.risk: Mobile behaviour is the requirement most often declared done from a resized desktop window. It is asserted at real viewport widths by a browser check.

nodes.label: I1017
nodes.summary: Live state is an overlay that degrades to nothing

acceptance_criteria: Live updates use the process's existing event transport rather than a new one
Live values are visually and structurally distinguishable from snapshot values
The static projection renders the useful equivalent — what the endpoint is, and that the value is available when a server runs — rather than an empty card
Reconnection is bounded and backs off, and a failed connection does not produce a request storm
facts.current_state: The process has a health capability and peers. No surface subscribes to anything.
facts.desired_state: Live values arrive over the existing transport, are visibly distinct from the snapshot, and are absent rather than stale where no backend answers.
non_scope: A transport invented for the Cockpit alongside one that already exists
A reconnect loop with no bound
facts.risk: Live overlays are where credentials leak into browsers. Everything sent to the client is an allowlisted safe field.
facts.why: Live state is what makes a control plane worth opening. It is also what makes a static page lie, so it has to be an overlay that is visibly absent rather than a field that is silently stale.

nodes.label: I1018
nodes.summary: The surface rules exist as checks, proved by making them fail

acceptance_criteria: A change to an authoritative source that leaves any derived surface stale fails the drift check, and the failure names the source to change
A public or developer-facing capability that is not discoverable through the generated interface fails, unless it declares itself internal
A capability with behaviour carries verification appropriate to its kind, decided by typed policy rather than by one rule for everything
A developer-facing capability resolves to canonical documentation, and the coverage is visible rather than only reported
The static and runtime representations must remain equal after runtime-only fields are removed, enforced by the parity test
Each rule has a negative test that proves the check fires, and CI executes every one
facts.current_state: Project rules exist with checks for derived files, projections, hot paths, benchmark coverage and scope. None concerns UI exposure, capability documentation or verification policy.
facts.desired_state: Each rule has a check, each check has a negative test that proves it fires, and CI runs all of them.
non_scope: A rule with no executable check
Requiring documentation or a test from purely descriptive metadata
Duplicating a constraint an existing rule already enforces
facts.risk: Five new rules can make ordinary contribution feel like litigation. Each policy is typed by capability kind so that a descriptive object is not asked for a behavioural test.
facts.why: Everything in this milestone decays the moment a change can land without a check noticing. A rule that exists only as a document is a suggestion wearing a uniform.

nodes.label: I1019
nodes.summary: One skill runs the whole loop, and is itself in the graph

acceptance_criteria: The skill sequences the existing commands rather than reimplementing their behaviour
It follows the existing skill contract and needs no special-casing to be registered
It appears in the graph, the interface and the search through the ordinary derivation
It is tested behaviourally, on a repository state where something is genuinely missing
facts.current_state: Skills are a registered kind with a contract. None covers this loop.
facts.desired_state: One skill does the whole loop, follows the existing skill contract, and appears in the graph, the interface and the search like everything else.
non_scope: Several thin skills where one is enough
A skill that reimplements what the commands already do rather than sequencing them
facts.risk: A skill that wraps commands adds a layer that can drift from them. It sequences and reports; it does not decide anything the commands do not.
facts.why: The loop this milestone creates should be runnable by a worker without knowing which command does which part. And a repository that models skills as data should have its own automation as one of them.

nodes.label: I1020
nodes.summary: The graph's health is answered by the doctor that already answers everything else

acceptance_criteria: The checks cover graph validity, identity uniqueness, relation resolution, projection freshness, required documentation and verification presence, and the absence of unsafe metadata
Every number reported is computed, not stated
The output is machine-readable and human-readable in the existing shapes
Each check delegates to the engine that already decides it
facts.current_state: The health capability aggregates index diagnostics, benchmark coverage and projection staleness.
facts.desired_state: The graph's verdicts join them, computed rather than asserted, in the same machine-readable and human-readable output.
non_scope: A separate diagnostic script or command for the Cockpit
A check that recomputes a verdict another engine already produces
facts.risk: Building the whole graph inside a blocking check makes the pre-commit hook slow enough to be bypassed, which the performance doctrine already refuses. Its cost is measured against that budget.

nodes.label: I1021
nodes.summary: A browser proves the interface, at the widths people use

acceptance_criteria: Desktop and mobile navigation, search and filtering, the detail view and graph initialisation are all exercised
Representative viewports from a narrow phone to a wide desktop are asserted, including the absence of horizontal overflow
The runtime-only surfaces appear when a backend is present and are not offered when it is not
Internal links resolve and the console is free of errors
Selectors are stable identifiers rather than presentational classes
facts.current_state: A probe script drives the Cockpit's routes and interactions in a real browser.
facts.desired_state: The probe covers the derived surfaces at representative viewports, uses stable selectors and runs in CI.
non_scope: Pixel comparison of a rendered graph
Selectors coupled to presentational class names
facts.risk: Browser tests are the flakiest thing in any suite. Bounded waits on stable selectors, and no sleeps.
facts.why: Everything in this milestone is finally judged by whether a person can open it. Server-side tests cannot see an overflowing table, a menu that does not open or a script that throws on load.

nodes.label: I1022
nodes.summary: Drift in any derived surface fails the build

acceptance_criteria: Every new artifact is part of the canonical target set and its check
A drift failure names the authoritative source to change, not only the generated file that differs
Generation is deterministic, so an unchanged repository never reports drift
CI executes the check on every change
facts.current_state: The generation check covers the existing target set.
facts.desired_state: The new artifacts are in the same set, and a drift failure names the source to change rather than the file that differs.
non_scope: A separate drift script for the new artifacts
facts.risk: A non-deterministic generator turns this check into noise within a day, and the response to noise is to disable the check.
facts.why: Generation without a check is a suggestion. This is the mechanism that makes every derived surface in this milestone actually derived.

nodes.label: I1023
nodes.summary: Nothing private reaches a published page

acceptance_criteria: Known credential variable names, credential-shaped values, raw authorization material and machine-absolute paths are all detected
A finding names the location and the kind and never the value
A negative test plants a synthetic marker and proves the check finds it
The check runs in CI on every change
facts.current_state: No such scan exists for the site or the Cockpit data.
facts.desired_state: One check inspects the generated data and the built site, reports findings by location and kind, and runs in CI.
non_scope: Printing any secret value while scanning
A general secret scanner competing with the repository's existing tooling
facts.objective: Scan the published graph, the static site and everything the client receives for credential material, private environment values and machine-absolute paths, and fail on a finding without printing it.
facts.risk: A scan tuned to be quiet finds nothing forever. The synthetic marker is what keeps it honest.
facts.why: This milestone publishes a description of everything the repository knows. That is exactly the artifact in which an accidental token or a developer's home directory would travel furthest.

nodes.label: I1024
nodes.summary: The interface has a weight, and it is measured

acceptance_criteria: The generated data size, the served HTML size, the initial script and style weight and the graph initialisation are all measured
The baselines live where the benchmark infrastructure already keeps them, with the environment recorded
Thresholds catch a material regression and tolerate ordinary growth, and the policy states which is which
Heavy libraries are absent from pages that do not use them, proved by measurement rather than by intent
facts.current_state: The benchmark infrastructure records distributions per command against a committed baseline. Nothing measures a page or an asset.
facts.desired_state: The interface's weight and initialisation are baselines like the commands', with thresholds that catch a real regression and ignore a byte.
non_scope: A new benchmark system beside the one that exists
A threshold so tight that ordinary content growth fails the build
facts.objective: Measure the generated data, the served HTML, the initial scripts and styles and the graph's initialisation, and hold them to budgets through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has.
facts.risk: Asset budgets provoke arguments about kilobytes. The threshold is set where it detects a category change, not a content edit.
facts.why: A derived interface grows with the repository by construction. Without a measured budget it becomes slow gradually, which is the way that never gets noticed.

nodes.label: I1025
nodes.summary: The federated model and its two projections are an architecture decision

acceptance_criteria: The record follows the repository's ADR format and frontmatter exactly and relates to the decisions it extends
It states the federated composition, the dual projection, progressive enhancement, availability as metadata and the conditional exposure of runtime surfaces
The alternatives — one central manifest, a client-side application fetching the API, a separate site generator — are recorded with why they were not taken
The consequences state what a new subsystem must do to appear, and what it costs when it does not
facts.current_state: ADR 12 establishes the Cockpit as a projection of the registry. ADR 13 establishes that web surfaces are discovered from their producers. Neither covers the composed graph or the static projection.
facts.desired_state: One record states the decision, extends rather than restates the two it follows, and says what would have to change to revisit it.
non_scope: Restating ADR 12 or ADR 13
An ADR that documents the implementation instead of the decision
facts.objective: Record the decision to compose the authoritative registries into one typed graph and to render it as two projections, with the alternatives that were real and the consequences that follow.
facts.risk: Written last, it becomes a summary of the code. It is written when the choice between composing and centralising is still open.

nodes.label: I1026
nodes.summary: The architecture explains itself, from inside itself

facts.current_state: The Cockpit has a document. The composed graph, the relation model and the contributor workflow have none.
facts.desired_state: One architecture document, reachable from the places a reader starts, and an interface that states its own mode, sources and revision.
non_scope: Duplicating the ADR's reasoning in prose
Repeating full instructions in every directory document instead of composing them
facts.objective: Document the graph, its sources, its relation model, its two projections and the contributor workflow, and let the interface say how it was generated and from what.
facts.risk: A document explaining a derivation goes stale faster than the derivation. Every value it states about the current repository is generated rather than typed.

nodes.label: I1027
nodes.summary: A synthetic capability proves the architecture instead of describing it

acceptance_criteria: The capability is registered only at its authoritative source, and no surface is edited
After generation it appears in the graph, the interface, the search, the navigation and the static projection
Omitting its required documentation or verification fails enforcement with a message naming what is missing
Supplying the evidence makes every check pass
The fixture is removed afterwards, or kept only where test fixtures belong
facts.current_state: Nothing proves the loop end to end.
facts.desired_state: One test registers a synthetic capability, generates, and asserts its appearance everywhere it should appear — and asserts the failure when its required evidence is missing.
non_scope: Leaving the synthetic fixture in the repository as if it were a real capability
Special-casing the fixture anywhere in the implementation
facts.risk: A fixture that the implementation learns to recognise proves nothing. It has to be ordinary in every respect.
facts.why: Every claim in this milestone reduces to one: adding something requires no edit to any surface. That is either demonstrable or it is marketing, and the demonstration is cheap.

nodes.label: I1028
nodes.summary: The inventories this replaces are removed, not left running beside it

acceptance_criteria: The inventories that are replaced are enumerated from the repository, not assumed, and each is either removed or justified as authoritative for something else
Every consumer reads the derivation after the removal
Nothing that was removed is reachable as a fallback path
The built site and the running interface show the same content as before the removal, except where the derivation is more complete
facts.current_state: Several surfaces assemble their own lists. Which ones exactly is a reconnaissance result, not an assumption.
facts.desired_state: Each replaced inventory is deleted, its consumers read the derivation, and nothing hand-written survives as a fallback.
non_scope: Deleting a list that is genuinely authoritative for something the graph does not model
Leaving a hand-written list in place as a fallback
facts.risk: Removing a list that quietly held something the graph does not model loses content. Each removal is checked against what the derivation actually produces.
facts.why: Two systems doing the same job is worse than either alone: the old one keeps working just well enough that nobody notices it has diverged. Migration is finished when the thing it replaced is gone.

nodes.label: I1029
nodes.summary: The gate refuses what would silently break the interface

acceptance_criteria: A stale derived surface, a missing required document, a missing required verification, a broken static link to a runtime-only surface and unsafe published metadata each fail the gate
The browser checks and the parity test run on every pull request
Caching keeps the added time proportionate, and the total is measured
No check added here lives outside the existing verification hierarchy
facts.current_state: The verification workflow runs the repository's existing checks.
facts.desired_state: The new checks belong to the same gate, run on every pull request, and the gate stays fast enough to be usable.
non_scope: A separate workflow for the interface checks
A gate slow enough that people work around it
facts.risk: Browser checks in CI are where a suite becomes unreliable. They run against a built artifact with bounded waits, or they do not run at all.
facts.why: Every mechanism in this milestone depends on failing loudly at merge time. Without the gate they are conventions, and conventions are the thing this repository builds machinery to avoid needing.

nodes.label: I1030
nodes.summary: The milestone is accepted on its evidence

acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of the milestone has evidence recorded against it
The coverage matrix baseline is recorded as a starting measurement rather than presented as a verdict
The contributor workflow runs exactly as documented on a clean checkout
Pre-existing failures, failures introduced here and failures fixed here are distinguished explicitly
Remaining limitations are stated rather than omitted
facts.current_state: Open.
facts.desired_state: Accepted with evidence against every criterion, with the coverage baseline and the limitations written where they will be found.
non_scope: Reporting a derived surface as proved without the artifact that proves it
facts.objective: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measurements are recorded with their environment, the contributor workflow runs as written, and the remaining gaps are stated.
facts.risk: The end of a large milestone is where intent gets recorded as outcome. Anything not demonstrated is written as a limitation.
facts.why: A milestone is accepted by its evidence. What a later reader has is the record, not this session.

nodes.label: I1031
nodes.summary: A served surface says which checkout it is serving

acceptance_criteria: The home page names the repository root and identity the process is serving, not only the surfaces it exposes
The interactive API shell names the same root, so a page fetched from one server cannot be mistaken for another's
The identity comes from the repository model rather than from a second inspection
No surface names the repository's location on the host: the identity says which checkout answered, never where it sits, and a test proves no served or published output carries an absolute path
The behaviour is exercised by a test that serves two roots and proves each surface names its own
facts.desired_state: Every served surface carries the repository root and identity it is answering for, close enough to the content that a reader sees it without asking for it.
non_scope: Publishing an absolute developer path to anything but a loopback surface
A second identity beside the one the repository model already holds
Changing what any surface serves; this changes only what it says about itself

nodes.label: I1101
nodes.summary: What this tool leaves behind, established by inspection rather than by memory

acceptance_criteria: Every path written or mutated outside `.ai/` and `.majordomus/` is listed with the code that writes it, found by inspection rather than by assumption
Each is classified as canonical, derived, generated, cache, runtime or accidental, with the reason
The classification says which paths the two-folder contract keeps as bridges, which move into a namespace and which stop existing
Where an existing mechanism already does what a later phase would add, it is named so the phase extends it rather than replacing it
The architectural decision is recorded in the repository's own ADR mechanism, not in prose beside it
facts.desired_state: One document records the actual footprint with its writer, its lifecycle and its justification, and names which of them the target architecture keeps, moves or removes.
non_scope: Moving anything; this issue changes no path
A rewrite of a subsystem discovered along the way
facts.risk: A forensic phase can become a rewrite the moment it finds something ugly. It records; the phases that follow change.

nodes.label: I1102
nodes.summary: The two namespaces are a typed contract, not a habit

acceptance_criteria: Each namespace declares what it holds, in typed and versioned form, generated from the canonical Rust types where generation is available
`.ai/` is defined as portable semantic material that keeps its meaning without this tool and across providers, and `.majordomus/` as control-plane state that must never hold a second copy of it
A check refuses an artifact placed in the namespace whose contract excludes it, and names both the path and the contract it violates
The skeleton a new repository receives is derived from the same declaration rather than being a parallel copy of it
facts.desired_state: The layout is a schema-backed declaration; a check reads it and refuses a path that contradicts it.
non_scope: A configuration file restating what a convention already fixes
Moving existing content; that is the migration issue
facts.risk: A layout schema can become a second description of the tree it describes. It declares intent and lifecycle; the tree remains what discovery finds.

nodes.label: I1103
nodes.summary: Whether a file is authored or derived is a field, not a naming convention

acceptance_criteria: Every generated artifact declares its generator, its version and the canonical inputs it derives from
Disposability is explicit, so a consumer can tell what may be deleted and rebuilt from what may not
A generated artifact is never read back as canonical input, and a check proves it
Authored artifacts are distinguishable from derived ones without consulting a path
facts.desired_state: Provenance and lifecycle are typed fields every artifact carries, and a consumer decides what it may do with a file by reading them.
non_scope: Replacing the existing banner mechanism where it already answers the question
A provenance field that repeats what the schema id already fixes
facts.risk: Recording inputs invites recording them by hand. The input list is derived from the generator, or it is not recorded.

nodes.label: I1104
nodes.summary: Both namespaces carry their contracts, all the way down

acceptance_criteria: Every directory of both namespaces carries a contract with valid typed front matter, and a missing one fails the existing validator
Each states purpose, ownership and lifecycle, the schemas that apply, and how its contents are discovered and extended
Contracts compose rather than repeat: a child adds to its ancestors and never restates them
The same mechanism serves both namespaces, with no second format
facts.current_state: ADR 0011 established that every directory of the layer carries a contract, and a validator enforces it under `.ai/`. `.majordomus/` has no such requirement.
facts.desired_state: The same validator covers both namespaces, and the effective context for an artifact composes from the contracts above it in either.
non_scope: A second contract format for the second namespace
Duplicating a parent's instructions in every child
facts.risk: Mechanical coverage produces mechanical documents. A contract that says nothing a reader could not guess is a cost with no benefit, and the review has to say so.

nodes.label: I1105
nodes.summary: The repository is discovered once, into one model

acceptance_criteria: One typed value carries what a consumer needs to know about a repository, composed from the registries that already own their parts
Discovery happens once per process, and a second consumer pays nothing for it
Nothing in the model requires a configuration file to state what inspection can establish
No consumer reads the filesystem for a fact the model already carries, proved by a check rather than by review
facts.desired_state: One discovery produces one typed value; consumers hold it rather than the filesystem.
non_scope: A second index beside the one that exists; this composes it
Discovery that reaches the network or builds anything
facts.risk: A model that knows everything is discovered slowly, and the environment entry pays that cost on every directory change. Its cost is measured in the same issue that makes it mandatory, not later.

nodes.label: I1106
nodes.summary: The registries are views of the model, not separate discoveries

acceptance_criteria: Each registry is derived from the model, and no consumer builds its own
Adding a schema-valid artifact under a discoverable namespace exposes it to every applicable consumer with no further registration, proved by a synthetic artifact in a test
A malformed artifact fails loudly with its path and its schema violation rather than vanishing from a listing
Ordering is deterministic, so two runs over one tree produce one answer
facts.current_state: Kinds are discovered by source classes and indexed; capabilities are declared and projected. The two are joined only in the composed graph, and other consumers still enumerate.
facts.desired_state: Every registry is a projection of the model, and a new artifact appears in the CLI, the API, MCP, the Cockpit, the documentation and search without anything being listed.
non_scope: A registry file that enumerates what discovery finds
Changing what any kind means; this changes where it is read from
facts.risk: Silent omission is the failure mode: an artifact that fails validation and simply does not appear is indistinguishable from one nobody wrote. It has to fail, not disappear.
facts.why: Registration by hand is the defect this repository has removed once per subsystem. Doing it once over one model is what stops the next subsystem from reinventing it.

nodes.label: I1107
nodes.summary: Discovery is deterministic, cached, and its cost is known

acceptance_criteria: Two discoveries over an unchanged tree produce structurally identical models, with no dependence on directory iteration order
The cache is keyed by the content it was derived from, so a stale entry costs a miss and never a wrong answer
Cold and warm discovery are benchmarked separately with a recorded baseline
A cache hit and a cache miss produce byte-identical output for every read-only command
facts.current_state: The layer's flattening is cached by content hash and the executable's phases are timed. The composed model's own cost has not been measured.
facts.desired_state: The cost is a benchmark with a baseline, the cache is keyed by the inputs, and a stale entry cannot be read for a changed tree.
non_scope: A cache that can serve a stale answer for a changed input
A persistent cache shared between repositories
facts.objective: Make one discovery over one tree produce one answer, cache it by what it was derived from, and measure what it costs — because everything downstream now pays that cost.
facts.risk: A cache is a second thing that can be believed. Keying it by content hash means a wrong key costs time, never correctness.
facts.why: A model every consumer reads is on the hot path of every command, including the ones that run when a person changes directory. An unmeasured spine becomes the reason the tool is avoided.

nodes.label: I1108
nodes.summary: The desired integration is a value, and the plan is a diff

acceptance_criteria: The desired integration is derived from the repository model, and a repository that already conforms produces an empty difference
The difference is a typed value that names every path it would create, modify or remove, and why
A dry run performs the same computation as an apply and mutates nothing
The apply performs exactly the difference and nothing else, proved by comparing the tree before and after against the plan
A mutation the plan did not name is a bug, and a test proves the apply cannot make one
facts.current_state: Initialisation writes a skeleton. Nothing computes what is missing, nothing reports what would change, and running it again is not a defined operation.
non_scope: Applying anything the dry run did not show
A desired state that depends on a configuration file rather than on the model
facts.objective: Compute what a repository's Majordomus integration should look like as a typed value, diff it against what the repository actually holds, and make the apply the smallest mutation that closes the gap.
facts.risk: A reconciler that computes what a repository should look like will eventually be wrong about one. Everything it would do outside the two namespaces must be visible before it is done.

nodes.label: I1109
nodes.summary: Everything placed outside the two namespaces is recorded, with what it was

acceptance_criteria: Every mutation outside the two namespaces is recorded with its path, its kind, the hash as written, the generator and version, and the prior state
A managed region records the markers that bound it, so the rest of the file is never in question
The ledger is typed and schema-backed, generated from the canonical type rather than hand-written
A path whose current hash does not match what the ledger recorded is reported as edited by a person, and no mutation proceeds on it silently
The ledger contains no secret and no absolute developer path
facts.current_state: Root documents carry generated blocks and provider bootstraps are written to the root. Nothing records that Majordomus put them there.
facts.desired_state: The ledger is the authority on what Majordomus owns outside its namespaces, and a mismatch between what it recorded and what is on disk stops a mutation rather than resolving it.
non_scope: Recording anything inside the two namespaces, which are owned by construction
A ledger a person is expected to edit
facts.risk: A ledger that drifts from the filesystem authorises deletions it cannot justify. The hash is what keeps it honest, and a mismatch has to stop the operation rather than warn about it.

nodes.label: I1110
nodes.summary: The second run changes nothing, and a test says so

acceptance_criteria: Reconciling a conforming repository twice leaves the tree byte-identical, including every generated artifact
The second run reports no change rather than reporting changes it then does not make
The test covers a repository that was already adopted, one adopted by an older version, and one where a person edited a bridge
A deliberate divergence makes the test fail, proving it can
facts.current_state: Initialisation is not idempotent and nothing measures whether it is.
facts.desired_state: A second reconciliation reports zero changes, the working tree is byte-identical, and a test fails the moment that stops being true.
non_scope: Achieving stillness by making the second run skip work it should do
Ignoring a difference because it is only in a generated file
facts.objective: Make reconciliation idempotent: running it against a conforming repository produces no change at all, and prove it with a test rather than with an observation.
facts.risk: The easy way to pass this test is to make the second run do nothing on principle. The test has to distinguish a reconciler that found nothing to do from one that did not look.

nodes.label: I1111
nodes.summary: Uninstall gives back exactly what was taken

acceptance_criteria: Every recorded mutation outside the two namespaces is reversed to the state the ledger recorded as prior
A managed region is removed without disturbing the rest of its file, and a file that exists only because Majordomus created it is removed whole
A bridge whose hash no longer matches is left in place and reported, never overwritten or deleted
The default leaves authored `.ai/` content untouched; removing generated state and removing authored content are separate, explicit requests
After the default removal, the repository is what it was before adoption apart from authored content, proved by comparing against a recorded starting state
facts.current_state: Nothing removes an adoption. What Majordomus wrote outside its namespaces can only be found by reading a diff.
facts.desired_state: One command reverses the ledger, one flag additionally removes generated state, and removing authored content is a separate decision the default never makes.
non_scope: Removing authored content under any default
A broad recursive delete of any path not named by the ledger
facts.objective: Implement removal that reverses every recorded mutation, refuses anything a person has since edited, and leaves authored knowledge in place unless removal is asked for separately and explicitly.
facts.risk: This is the operation where a mistake destroys somebody's work. Every deletion is justified by a ledger entry and a matching hash, or it does not happen.

nodes.label: I1112
nodes.summary: What touches the root is two small blocks, and they never change again

acceptance_criteria: Each bridge is bounded by markers, recorded in the ledger, and carries no logic — only a reference to where the canonical material lives
Upgrading the tool leaves the bridges byte-identical, proved by reconciling with a newer version against an older adoption
A bridge is created only when the surface genuinely requires a root file; where a tool can be configured programmatically, nothing is written
The environment bridge is one stable line whose target lives under `.majordomus/`
facts.current_state: Root documents carry generated blocks whose content is regenerated as the layer changes, and provider bootstraps are written to the root.
facts.desired_state: A bridge names where the truth lives and stops. Upgrading Majordomus does not rewrite it, because there is nothing version-dependent inside it.
non_scope: Repository-domain logic in any root file
A bridge whose content depends on the version of the tool that wrote it
facts.risk: Every provider that wants a root file argues that its file is special. The answer is the same one: the file is an adapter, and its content is derived.

nodes.label: I1113
nodes.summary: Entering a directory is local, bounded and silent about the network

acceptance_criteria: The entry path performs no network request, no build and no mutation of a tracked file
Its cost is measured against a declared budget, cold and warm, and a regression fails the check
What it displays is derived from the same model every other consumer reads, not from a parallel inspection
A repository that has not been adopted produces no error and no noise
facts.current_state: The environment integration exists and its shape is described in the supplied reference. Its cost under the new model is unmeasured.
facts.desired_state: The entry path reads cached, local state, its cost is benchmarked against a stated budget, and a regression fails a check rather than being noticed.
non_scope: Any network call, any build, any repository mutation on the entry path
A banner that recomputes what a cache already holds
facts.objective: Keep environment entry — the direnv hook, the banner, the shell integration — local, bounded and free of build and network work, and measure it against a declared budget.
facts.risk: Cheap on this machine is not cheap on a cold cache over a network filesystem. The budget is measured on a cold cache, and the environment it was measured on is recorded with it.
facts.why: This runs every time a person changes directory. A second of it is a tax on every action of the day, and a network call in it turns a flaky connection into a broken shell.

nodes.label: I1114
nodes.summary: A provider is an adapter over the model, and adding one is an implementation

acceptance_criteria: Every provider representation is derived from the model and declares its provenance
Adding a provider is one implementation of the adapter contract, with no edit to the layer and no new list
A provider that can be configured programmatically produces no repository file at all
Where a root file is unavoidable it is a managed bridge with recorded ownership, and its content is derived
facts.current_state: Provider bootstraps are generated from the registry, which is the right shape, but they land at the root and their ownership is not recorded.
facts.desired_state: Adapters are generated into the control-plane namespace, bridged at the root only where a tool truly requires a root file, and a new provider is a trait implementation.
non_scope: Provider semantics in the canonical layer
A provider list maintained by hand
facts.risk: An adapter layer can grow provider-shaped holes in the model beneath it. The check is whether the model would still be complete if every adapter were deleted.

nodes.label: I1115
nodes.summary: Completion comes from the command model, not from a second list

acceptance_criteria: Completion data is derived from the command model with no second enumeration
A command added to the model is completable after the ordinary generation, with no further edit
The refresh is cached state under the control-plane namespace and never a tracked-file mutation
Whatever the entry path does for completion stays inside the entry budget
facts.current_state: The CLI is declared once and its reference is generated. Completion, where it exists, is not derived from that declaration.
facts.desired_state: Completion is generated from the command model, refreshed as safe cached state, and never enumerated by hand.
non_scope: A completion script maintained by hand
Regenerating completion on the environment-entry path if it costs more than the budget allows
facts.objective: Derive shell completion from the same command model the CLI and its documentation already come from, so that a new command is completable without anything being listed.
facts.risk: Completion is where a fast path tempts a shortcut list. Deriving it is cheap only if the model is already cached; otherwise the budget decides.
facts.why: A completion script is the least visible copy of a command list and therefore the one that drifts furthest. It is also the one people notice, because a missing completion reads as a missing feature.

nodes.label: I1116
nodes.summary: This repository's own footprint moves, through the reconciler

acceptance_criteria: Every move goes through a recorded migration, previewable as a dry run before it is applied
Compatibility is preserved for the paths other work depends on, or the break is deliberate, documented and migrated
After the migration this repository conforms to its own contract, checked by the same validator a foreign repository would face
Nothing that was working before stops working, proved by the full suite rather than by inspection
facts.current_state: The footprint is what phase one recorded. Nothing has moved.
facts.desired_state: The repository conforms to its own contract, every move is recorded, and nothing that was working stopped working.
non_scope: A broad recursive delete anywhere
Moving user-authored content without recording where it went
A shell script that performs the migration outside the reconciler

nodes.label: I1117
nodes.summary: The hand-maintained lists are removed, not left running beside the derivation

acceptance_criteria: The lists that are replaced are enumerated from the repository rather than assumed, and each is removed or justified as authoritative for something else
Every consumer reads the derivation after the removal, and nothing removed remains reachable as a fallback
What the interfaces show is the same as before the removal, except where the derivation is more complete
A check refuses a new enumeration of a discoverable namespace
facts.current_state: Several such lists have been removed already; the rest are what phase one recorded and what the derivation makes redundant.
facts.desired_state: Each replaced list is deleted, its consumers read the derivation, and nothing survives as a fallback.
non_scope: Deleting a list that is genuinely authoritative for something the model does not hold
Leaving a hand-written list in place as a fallback
facts.objective: Find every list that enumerates what discovery already finds — indexes, menus, route tables, provider lists, documentation catalogues — and remove it, so that one derivation is the only one.
facts.risk: A list quietly holding something the model does not carry loses that content when it goes. Each removal is checked against what the derivation actually produces, item by item.

nodes.label: I1118
nodes.summary: Every invariant of this milestone is a rule with a check that runs

acceptance_criteria: Majordomus-owned persistent state outside the two namespaces fails a check unless the ledger records it as a bridge
A secondary registry enumerating a discoverable namespace fails a check
A generated artifact without provenance, or read back as canonical input, fails a check
A mutation outside the two namespaces without a ledger entry fails a check
A non-idempotent reconciliation fails a check
Each rule has a negative test proving its check fires, and CI executes every one
facts.current_state: The invariants exist as prose in the mission and as behaviour in the code. No rule states them and no check enforces them.
facts.desired_state: Each invariant is a rule with a check, each check has a negative test, and CI runs all of them.
non_scope: A rule with no executable check
Restating a constraint an existing rule already enforces
facts.risk: Seven rules for one milestone is a lot of doctrine. Any constraint an existing rule already covers is referenced rather than restated, and the review has to insist on that.
facts.why: Everything in this milestone decays the moment a change can land without a check noticing. A rule with no check is a suggestion, and this repository has a rule saying exactly that.

nodes.label: I1119
nodes.summary: The budgets are measured, and a regression fails rather than being noticed

acceptance_criteria: Discovery, reconciliation, the dry run and the environment entry are benchmark targets with recorded baselines
The thresholds are policy data, and the check names the target, both values and the threshold when it fails
The environment it was measured on is recorded with each baseline
A material regression fails; a byte does not
facts.current_state: The benchmark infrastructure records distributions per command against a committed baseline. The new paths are not among its targets.
facts.desired_state: Each new path is a benchmark target with a recorded baseline and a threshold that catches a material regression while tolerating ordinary growth.
non_scope: A second benchmark system
A threshold so tight that ordinary content growth fails the build
facts.objective: Measure what this architecture costs — discovery, reconciliation, the environment entry, the generated artifacts — and hold each to a budget derived from its measured baseline.
facts.risk: Wall-clock thresholds are noisy across machines. The structural counters gate strictly and the timings conservatively, as the existing performance doctrine already decided.
facts.why: A spine every consumer reads is a cost every consumer pays. Measured once and then never again, it grows until somebody works around the tool instead of using it.

nodes.label: I1120
nodes.summary: A refusal says what to do about it

acceptance_criteria: A refusal names the file or path, what was found, what was expected and the command that repairs it
An edited bridge, a ledger mismatch, a non-conforming path and a plan touching something unowned each have their own message rather than a shared generic one
The messages are exercised by tests, so a change that degrades one is caught
Machine-readable output carries the same detail as the human-readable form
facts.current_state: Errors in the executable carry structured detail in places and a bare message in others. The new operations have no convention yet.
facts.desired_state: Each refusal is actionable, and a person who has never read this code can act on it without reading this code.
non_scope: A second diagnostics framework
A message that reports a condition without naming the repair
facts.objective: Make every refusal in this subsystem name the source of truth, what was observed, what was expected and the command that repairs it — through the diagnostics framework that already exists.
facts.risk: Message quality is the first thing to decay under time pressure and the last thing anybody tests. Testing the messages is what keeps them.

nodes.label: I1121
nodes.summary: Every surface shows the integration from the one model

acceptance_criteria: The integration reads are declared once and appear in the CLI, the API, the API document, MCP, the Cockpit and the generated reference with no second registration
No mutating operation is exposed to an untrusted surface; adoption and removal stay with the trusted command line
The Cockpit shows what is adopted, what is owned and what a reconciliation would change, from that declaration
The published documentation derives its integration reference from the same model, with no retyped value
facts.current_state: The capability registry already projects declared operations into every surface. The integration state is not among them.
facts.desired_state: One declaration exposes the integration reads, and every surface derives from it as it does for everything else.
non_scope: A mutating integration operation exposed to unauthenticated HTTP or to a browser
A hand-edited API document, route table or documentation list
facts.risk: Showing what a reconciliation would change means running the plan on a request. Its cost belongs to the budget, and a read that builds a plan has to say so.
facts.why: The question a person asks about an integration is what it did to my repository, and they will ask it wherever they happen to be. Answering it four ways is how the four answers begin to differ.

nodes.label: I1122
nodes.summary: A foreign repository, adopted, upgraded and given back

acceptance_criteria: Adoption of a repository with no prior Majordomus state adds the two namespaces and the declared bridges, and nothing else, verified against the tree rather than against the report
The second adoption changes nothing
An adoption made by an older version reconciles forward without rewriting a bridge that did not need to change
A bridge edited by a person is refused rather than overwritten, and reported
Removal returns the repository to what it was, apart from authored content, compared against a recorded starting state
The fixture is ordinary in every respect and nothing in the implementation recognises it
facts.current_state: Nothing has been adopted anywhere but here.
facts.desired_state: One test drives the whole lifecycle on a foreign fixture and asserts each stage, including the ones designed to refuse.
non_scope: A fixture the implementation recognises as a test
Declaring success from the exit code of an adoption
facts.risk: An end-to-end test with a fixture the implementation special-cases proves nothing. The fixture has to be indistinguishable from a real repository.

nodes.label: I1123
nodes.summary: The milestone is accepted on its evidence

acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of the milestone has evidence recorded against it
The measured footprint of an adoption is recorded — every path, with its namespace and its owner
The budgets are recorded with the machine and environment they were measured on
The documented adoption and removal run exactly as written on a clean checkout
Pre-existing failures, failures introduced here and failures fixed here are distinguished explicitly
Remaining limitations are stated rather than omitted
facts.current_state: Open.
facts.desired_state: Accepted with evidence against every criterion, with the footprint, the budgets and the limitations written where they will be found.
non_scope: Reporting a mechanism as proved without the artifact that proves it
facts.risk: The end of a long milestone is where intent gets recorded as outcome. Anything not demonstrated is written as a limitation.
facts.why: A milestone is accepted by its evidence. What a later reader has is the record, not this session.

nodes.label: I1201
nodes.summary: An identity provider is a declarative object, and Google and Facebook are two of them

acceptance_criteria: The schema expresses one flow shape, and both objects validate against it without a per-provider escape hatch
Credentials are named, never carried: each object states the environment variable names and holds no value
The directory satisfies the recursive README and front-matter doctrine of the layer
The allow-list is generated from the schema by majordomus generate rather than written by hand
majordomus doctor reports the new kind and both objects with no diagnostic
facts.current_state: There is no identity kind, no .ai/repo/identity directory and no notion of a provider anywhere in the layer or the executable.
non_scope: Any Rust code that reads the objects, which is I1202
A client secret, a client id or any credential value in any file of the repository
A provider-specific field that only one of the two objects can use

nodes.label: I1202
nodes.summary: One typed provider model reads the objects, and no code names a provider

acceptance_criteria: The provider set is discovered from the directory, validated, and ordered deterministically
A provider with absent credentials is unavailable with a stated reason, and the reason reaches the surfaces
No provider identifier appears in the executable's source outside test fixtures
The read is declared once as a capability and appears in CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and docs with no second registration
facts.current_state: I1201 has the objects; nothing reads them.
non_scope: The HTTP flow, which is I1203
Reading a credential value into any type that is serialised, cached, logged or rendered
facts.risk: Resolving credentials at load makes the model unusable in any context that serialises it. They are resolved at the moment of the flow and never held.

nodes.label: I1203
nodes.summary: One flow serves every provider, and it refuses everything it did not start

acceptance_criteria: State and nonce are single-use, expiring, and bound to the provider they were issued for
The identity token is verified for issuer, audience, expiry and nonce before any session exists
A callback whose state was not issued by this server is refused without a session and without a redirect that leaks the parameters
The redirect target after sign-in is validated against the surface's own origin rather than taken from the request
Every refusal path has a test, and the tests run without contacting either provider
facts.current_state: I1202 gives the providers; there is no flow, no route and no verification.
non_scope: Storing anything about the reader beyond the session of I1204
A provider-specific branch anywhere in the flow
facts.risk: An open redirect and an unvalidated state are the two classic defects of this flow. Both are tested as refusals rather than assumed.

nodes.label: I1204
nodes.summary: The session is signed, short, and revocable from the server

acceptance_criteria: The cookie is signed with a key that comes from the environment and is absent from every artifact
Secure is set whenever the surface is served over anything but loopback, and the decision comes from the surface rather than from a constant
Sign-out revokes server-side, and a revoked session is refused even if the cookie is replayed
Expiry is enforced on the server, not only in the cookie's attributes
facts.current_state: No cookie, no session, no signing key handling.
facts.desired_state: A session exists as long as it is meant to, survives a restart only if that is the stated decision, and is gone from the server the moment sign-out is called.
non_scope: A session store shared between deployments
Remembering anything about the reader between sessions
facts.risk: A signing key with a compiled-in default is a signing key that ships. Its absence is a refusal to issue sessions, not a fallback.
facts.why: A cookie that only the browser can invalidate cannot be signed out of, and a session that carries claims in its payload cannot be revoked when the provider set changes underneath it.

nodes.label: I1205
nodes.summary: Identity is resolved once, in the router, and every surface reads it from there

acceptance_criteria: Exactly one place reads the session cookie, proved by a test that fails when a second appears
The Cockpit shows who is signed in and offers sign-out, from the resolved caller rather than from its own read
The MCP surface receives the same caller as the HTTP API for the same connection
An anonymous caller is a value, not an absence, so no surface can forget to handle it
facts.current_state: I1204 issues sessions; nothing reads them outside the flow.
facts.desired_state: A request carries a resolved caller — anonymous or identified — from the router onward, and a handler cannot be written that skips the resolution.
non_scope: Roles, groups or permissions beyond identified and anonymous
A second resolution in any surface
facts.risk: The Cockpit is the surface most likely to re-read the cookie for convenience. The test that forbids a second read is what keeps it honest.

nodes.label: I1206
nodes.summary: What an anonymous reader may do is derived from the effect classification, not from a list

acceptance_criteria: The policy states the requirement per effect class, and no route names its own requirement
A capability added with a mutating effect is refused to an anonymous caller with no edit to the HTTP layer, proved by a test capability
The OpenAPI document carries the security scheme and marks the operations that require it, generated rather than written
The Cockpit disables what the caller may not invoke and states the reason it is disabled
facts.current_state: Every route is served to everyone; the fly-deployment milestone therefore forbids exposing any mutating operation to the browser.
facts.desired_state: Adding a capability inherits its exposure from its effect class, and a capability that mutates cannot be reached anonymously without a policy change that is visible as one.
non_scope: A per-route authorisation table in any format
Granting a signed-in reader anything the effect policy has not classified
facts.risk: This issue depends on the effect classification being trustworthy. Where a capability's class is wrong, the fix is the classification, never an exception in the router.

nodes.label: I1207
nodes.summary: No credential reaches any output, and hostile provider metadata renders safely

acceptance_criteria: The sentinel sweep covers every output surface the repository produces, enumerated from the registry rather than listed by hand where that is possible
A deliberate regression that renders a secret is caught by the test, proved by a negative case
Hostile provider metadata renders as text on every surface, with no escape and no truncation that hides it
The gate runs in CI on every change
facts.current_state: No credentials exist yet, so no test can leak one.
facts.desired_state: A sentinel test runs in CI and fails loudly if any future change routes a credential into an output.
non_scope: Weakening the assertion to the outputs that happen to pass today
facts.risk: A sweep that enumerates outputs by hand will miss the surface added after it. Where the registry can enumerate them, it does.
facts.why: Every other guarantee of this milestone is a claim until a test tries to break it, and a credential that leaks once has leaked permanently.

nodes.label: I1208
nodes.summary: Adding a provider is one file, removing one is one deletion, and both are executed rather than described

acceptance_criteria: A synthetic provider dropped into the directory appears on every applicable surface with no source edit, proved by a test
Removing a provider object removes it from every surface, and sessions pinned to that issuer are refused
The documentation names the file to write and the file to delete, and cites the tests that execute both
A rule states that a provider fact may not be stated outside its object, with a check CI executes
facts.current_state: Nothing is documented and nothing performs the lifecycle.
facts.desired_state: The add and the remove are both proved by tests, and the documentation states the one-file operation because a test executes it.
non_scope: A migration path for sessions issued by a provider that has been struck, beyond revoking them
facts.risk: The removal half is the half that is skipped, and it is the half the operator asked for.

nodes.label: I1301
nodes.summary: A workspace is a declared object of the layer; only its content is local

acceptance_criteria: The object states vendor, upstream workspace identity, display name, the authorisation the operator asserts, the browser profile reference by name, and the expected capability set
Keys are closed by share/allow/workspace.txt and an unknown key is refused
The directory carries a context README stating what is authoritative and what is generated, per ADR 0011
The object is listed and read through the existing object surface with no code that special-cases it
No secret value and no credential name appears in the object or its schema
facts.current_state: No workspace kind, no .ai/repo/workspaces directory, no allow file and no schema exist.
non_scope: Any synced content; the store is I1303
Any credential, cookie or token value; the declaration names a profile, it does not hold one
Any Rust that special-cases the kind
facts.risk: A schema written for ChatGPT becomes a ChatGPT file with a generic name. It has to state only what a second vendor would plausibly restate, and push everything else into a named vendor block.

nodes.label: I1302
nodes.summary: Identity, provenance and support level are typed fields, not prose

acceptance_criteria: A local identity is reproducible from vendor and upstream identity alone and never depends on a display title
Every record states its transport, its acquisition mode and its support level as enumerated values
A content hash distinguishes a changed record from a re-observed one
A record gone upstream is tombstoned with a stamp, never removed silently
The schema carries a version and an unknown version is refused rather than parsed
facts.current_state: Nothing exists. The repository's own kinds compute identity generically from declared fields (index.rs identity_of) and that mechanism does not reach local content.
facts.risk: Over-modelling. The enumerations must be the ones a consumer actually branches on; a taxonomy nobody reads is a cost with no reader.

nodes.label: I1303
nodes.summary: The store is bounded, measured and invisible to every published projection

acceptance_criteria: The store layout and the checkpoint are described by a schema, not by a comment
A retention cap is stated in policy.yaml and doctor reports the store against it, in the shape the three existing stanzas use
A gate fails if the site build, the generated documentation or any published projection names a path under .ai/local/workspaces/
A test case proves the gate fails when the boundary is crossed deliberately
facts.current_state: No store, no cap, no stanza. .ai/local/ is git-ignored at .gitignore:55 and mj_validate_ai_layout fails the pre-commit hook if a file there is tracked.
non_scope: Declaring the store as a knowledge-sources class; ADR 0025 rejected it and the reasons are recorded there
Any adapter that writes into the store
facts.objective: Declare the layout of .ai/local/workspaces/, its checkpoint file, its retention cap in policy and the doctor stanza that measures it, and prove with a gate that nothing published ever reaches it.
facts.risk: A cap chosen from taste rather than measurement will either never fire or fire on the first real sync. It has to be stated in terms of what the operator's own workspace actually holds.

nodes.label: I1304
nodes.summary: The browser transport is the one this repository already drives

acceptance_criteria: The transport attaches to an explicitly configured, already-authenticated browser profile and refuses to guess one
Observation is scoped to the origins the workspace declaration names; traffic to any other origin is never recorded
Authorisation headers, cookies and set-cookie values are redacted before an observation is written anywhere
The existing UI and cockpit consumers use the same launcher, so the repository has one answer to how it starts a browser
Absent Chrome or absent node_modules, the command skips with the defined exit code the repository already uses rather than failing
facts.current_state: The two existing consumers each inline their own chromium.launch; no shared launcher was factored out. Neither targets an authenticated third-party session.
non_scope: Any credential written to disk, including a copied cookie jar or a profile archive
Any interaction with authentication, multi-factor prompts or anti-abuse controls
DOM scraping where a network observation answers the same question

nodes.label: I1305
nodes.summary: An observed contract has a fingerprint, a compatibility state and a fixture

acceptance_criteria: Every observed operation has a fingerprint over its shape and a compatibility state
A mismatched shape fails closed; nothing partial is persisted
A degraded contract falls back to the browser transport where one exists, and reports unavailability where none does
Fixtures are sanitised at capture time and CI replays them with no network and no account
Promoting a new contract requires a person and a passing test, and the mechanism cannot do it alone
facts.current_state: Nothing exists.
non_scope: Hardcoding any endpoint path taken from a prompt, a gist or documentation rather than from observed authorised traffic
Automatic promotion of a new observed shape
facts.risk: A fixture is a recording of private conversation. Sanitisation that runs after capture is sanitisation that has already failed; it runs before anything reaches disk.
facts.why: A vendor's undocumented surface is not a contract and will change. The failure this must prevent is not the loud one; it is a parse that half succeeds and writes plausible nonsense into the store.

nodes.label: I1306
nodes.summary: A sync resumes, repeats itself without harm, and says how fresh it is

acceptance_criteria: A second run over an unchanged workspace leaves the store byte-identical
An interrupted run resumes from its checkpoint without re-fetching what it already had
Every change records the acquisition mode that produced it, and a poll is never reported as a push
A run is bounded by count and by wall clock and says what it did not reach
Replaying a captured run over fixtures reproduces the same store
facts.current_state: Nothing exists.
non_scope: Any write to the vendor
Watch semantics that call polling a subscription
